definition_zh: 困难；难题；困境；费力
definition_en: the state of being hard, or a hard problem
core_image: 一块搬不动的大石头挡在路上
scene: 搬新家那天，客厅的旧沙发卡在楼梯口。 We had difficulty moving the old sofa down the stairs.
sceneCN: 这里 difficulty 是「费力、困难」（第 1 个义项：做起来吃力）；句意是我们搬旧沙发下楼很吃力。

derivatives.zh: difficulty 的形容词形式，义为「困难的」
由 difficult 加 -ly 构成，义为「困难地」

senses.title: The state of being hard
senses.definition: the fact that something needs much effort
senses.definitionCN: 某事需要很大努力的情况
senses.example: She read the long English story without much difficulty.
senses.exampleCN: 她毫不费力地读完了那个长长的英语故事。
senses.why: The Latin ending -tas names a state, so difficulty is the name of the pushing-back feeling you meet in a hard task.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语后缀 -tas 表示状态，difficulty 便给难事带来的「顶劲」起了名字。

senses.title: A hard problem or trouble
senses.definition: something hard to deal with, or a problem
senses.definitionCN: 难以处理的事情或麻烦
senses.example: The map had one difficulty: it did not show the small bridge.
senses.exampleCN: 这张地图有个问题：没标出那座小桥。
senses.why: A state of being hard soon becomes a thing you can point at, so the word names each single hard spot.
senses.whyCN: 「难」的状态很快变成可以指认的东西，于是这个词也能指一个个具体的难点。

senses.title: Money trouble or trouble in life
senses.definition: problems with money or with life
senses.definitionCN: 钱或生活上的难处
senses.example: His family had difficulty paying the school fees last year.
senses.exampleCN: 去年他家交学费有困难。
senses.why: Hard states in daily life usually start with money, so the word reached into bills and debts.
senses.whyCN: 生活里的难处多半从钱开始，这个词便延伸到账单与欠债上。

intro.en: Difficulty keeps its Latin shape almost unchanged.
intro.cn: difficulty 几乎原样保留了拉丁语的样子。

items.en: Latin had difficultas, later written difficultas with a c, from difficilis (not easy).
items.cn: 拉丁语有 difficultas，出自 difficilis（不容易）。

items.en: The word was built on dis- (not) plus facilis (easy), from facere (to do).
items.cn: 它由 dis-（不）加 facilis（容易做的）构成，而 facilis 出自 facere（做）。

items.en: Old French carried difficulte into medieval Europe.
items.cn: 古法语以 difficulte 把这个词带入中世纪欧洲。

items.en: English took it in the fourteenth century as difficulte, then difficulty.
items.cn: 十四世纪英语借入 difficulte，后写作 difficulty。

items.en: The plural difficulties names every hard spot one by one.
items.cn: 复数 difficulties 把一个个难点逐一指名。

note.en: These words name troubles and the difficulty family.
note.cn: 这些词指称麻烦以及 difficulty 词族。

entries.definition: adjective: hard to do
an ability, same Latin root
ease, or a building
shy, different root
entries.definitionCN: 羞怯的（拼写相近，词源不同）

entries.definition: more than one hard problem
a problem or worry
a hard question to solve
a hard fight or effort
a barrier to jump over
freedom from difficulty

normalIntro.en: Use the heavy stone and the have difficulty pattern.
normalIntro.cn: 用「大石头」画面和 have difficulty 句型来记。

normal.en: have difficulty in doing is the classic exam pattern.
normal.cn: have difficulty in doing 是经典考点句型。

normal.en: with difficulty means slowly and hard; without difficulty means easily.
normal.cn: with difficulty 是费力地，without difficulty 是轻松地。

normal.en: difficult is the adjective; difficulty adds -y for the noun.
normal.cn: difficult 是形容词，difficulty 加 -y 变名词。

normal.en: facilities are easy things; difficulties are hard things.
normal.cn: facility 是「容易」的近亲，difficulty 是「难」。

normal.en: Picture a stone you cannot lift.
normal.cn: 想象一块你搬不动的石头。

abstract.en: Feel your arms shake while pushing a heavy box.
abstract.cn: 体会推重箱子时手臂发抖的感觉。

abstract.en: See a test paper with one huge blank question.
abstract.cn: 想象一张考卷上留着一整道空白大题。

abstract.en: Hear a parent sigh over the bills at night.
abstract.cn: 听家长夜里对着账单轻轻叹气。

examples.en: I had difficulty finding the library, so I asked a policeman.
examples.cn: 我很难找到图书馆，于是问了一位警察。

examples.en: He climbed the wall with great difficulty.
examples.cn: 他非常吃力地爬上了那堵墙。

examples.en: Many families faced financial difficulties this winter.
examples.cn: 今年冬天许多家庭面临经济困难。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「弟非靠你」——弟弟非要靠你帮忙才行，说明他遇到了困难

root: 来自拉丁语 difficultas（困难），dis-（不）+ facilis（容易做的）；与 difficult 同根。

sensesIntro.en: Difficulty names the hard state, then each hard spot, then money trouble.
sensesIntro.cn: difficulty 先指「难」的状态，再指一个个难点，最后指经济上的难处。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a heavy stone on the road
core.cn: 核心意象：路上一块搬不动的石头

branches.en: The feel of something hard
branches.cn: 做难事时吃力的感觉

branches.en: A single hard spot to fix
branches.cn: 一个待解决的难点

branches.cn: 生活里的钱的问题

branches.cn: 从状态到被点名的难题

latinIntro.en: The Latin noun difficultas became the English word directly.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语名词 difficultas 直接演变成英语词。

definition_zh: 剪刀；剪式动作
definition_en: a cutting tool with two blades joined in the middle, or a scissor-like movement in sport
core_image: 桌上摊着彩纸，一把银色剪刀停在剪了一半的星星边
scene: 她拿起剪刀，把彩纸剪成星星。 She picked up the scissors and cut the paper into stars.
sceneCN: 这里 scissors 是「剪刀」（第 1 个义项）；句意：她拿起剪刀，把彩纸剪成星星。

derivatives.zh: 剪；用剪刀剪
剪式踢腿
剪式夹持

senses.title: A cutting tool
senses.definition: a tool with two blades joined in the middle that cuts when closed
senses.definitionCN: 中间相连、合拢时切割的两片刀刃工具
senses.example: These scissors are sharp.
senses.exampleCN: 这把剪刀很锋利。
senses.why: The core sense is the everyday cutting tool.
senses.whyCN: 核心义是日常切割工具。

senses.title: A scissor movement
senses.definition: a movement or hold in which two parts cross like blades
senses.definitionCN: 两部分像刀刃一样交叉的动作或夹持
senses.example: He won the match with a scissors hold.
senses.exampleCN: 他用剪式夹持赢得了比赛。
senses.why: The tool's crossing shape names a movement in sport.
senses.whyCN: 工具交叉的形状被用来命名体育动作。

intro.en: Scissors comes from Latin cisoria, cutting tools, from caedere, to cut.
intro.cn: scissors 源自拉丁语 cisoria（切割工具），来自 caedere（切）。

items.en: Caedere meant to cut or strike.
items.cn: caedere 意为切或砍。

items.en: Cisoria meant cutting tools.
items.cn: cisoria 意为切割工具。

items.en: Cisoires named a pair of cutting blades.
items.cn: cisoires 指成对的切割刀片。

items.en: Sisoures entered English as a plural word.
items.cn: sisoures 以复数形式进入英语。

items.en: Scissors keeps its plural form for one tool.
items.cn: 现代英语中 scissors 指一件工具却保留复数形式。

note.en: Scissors is compared with similar-looking words and with other cutting tools.
note.cn: 把 scissors 与形近词以及其他切割工具作比较。

entries.definition: to cut with scissors
to make a hissing sound
an official count of people
large scissors for cutting plants or metal
tools for cutting hair or nails
a tool or person that cuts

normalIntro.en: Scissors looks plural because it names two joined blades.
normalIntro.cn: scissors 看似复数，因为它指两片相连的刀刃。

normal.en: A pair of scissors is one tool.
normal.cn: a pair of scissors 指一件工具。

normal.en: Nail scissors are small and curved.
normal.cn: 指甲剪小而弯曲。

normal.en: Cut paper with scissors.
normal.cn: 用剪刀剪纸。

normal.en: Scissor is also a verb meaning to cut.
normal.cn: scissor 也可作动词，意为剪。

normal.en: Running with scissors is dangerous.
normal.cn: 拿着剪刀跑很危险。

abstract.en: Two blades cross, and the crossing gives the word its shape.
abstract.cn: 两片刀刃交叉，交叉的形状赋予这个词形象。

abstract.en: The plural form survives because the tool is made of two parts.
abstract.cn: 复数形式保留下来，因为这件工具由两部分组成。

abstract.en: The cutting action becomes a name for scissor movements.
abstract.cn: 切割动作又成为剪式动作的名称。

examples.en: Cut the thread with scissors.
examples.cn: 用剪刀剪断线。

examples.en: The child dropped the scissors.
examples.cn: 孩子把剪刀掉了。

examples.en: She keeps scissors in the drawer.
examples.cn: 她把剪刀放在抽屉里。

dict_mnemonic.text: scissors 来自拉丁语 caedere（切），原指切割工具；英语里常用复数形式 a pair of scissors。

root: 源自拉丁语 cisoria（切割工具），来自 caedere（切），核心义「成对刀片构成的切割工具」。

sensesIntro.en: Scissors means a cutting tool with two joined blades, or a crossing movement in sport.
sensesIntro.cn: scissors 意为两片刀刃相连的切割工具，或体育中的交叉剪式动作。

core.en: Two blades that cut by crossing.
core.cn: 通过交叉来切割的两片刀刃。

branches.en: A hand tool for cutting paper or cloth.
branches.cn: 剪纸或剪布的手持工具。

branches.en: A crossing hold or kick in sport.
branches.cn: 体育中的交叉夹持或踢腿。

branches.en: Both uses share the image of two crossing parts.
branches.cn: 两种用法都共享两部分交叉的形象。

branches.en: The tool's shape gives the movement its name.

intro.cn: scissors 构成表示工具与体育动作的复合词。

definition_zh: 牙；牙齿；齿状物；（齿轮的）齿
definition_en: one of the hard white parts in the mouth used for biting and chewing, or a pointed part shaped like one
core_image: 一排白牙咬住硬纸的边角，发出清脆的一声
scene: 灯下照着镜子里张开的口，牙刷停在最后一颗臼齿上。 He brushed each tooth slowly, counting them as he went.
sceneCN: 这里 tooth 就是嘴里的「牙齿」（第 1 个义项：口腔中用于咀嚼的坚硬白色器官）；句意为他把每颗牙慢慢刷过去，边刷边数。画面里有镜子、牙刷与张口的动作。

pos.zh: 名词：齿状物；（齿轮等的）齿

derivatives.zh: 不规则复数形式，义为「牙齿（复数）」
加 -less 构成，义为「无牙的；不起作用的」
加 -y 构成，义为「露齿的；牙齿显眼的」
与 ache 合成，义为「牙痛」

senses.title: The white part in the mouth
senses.definition: one of the hard calcified structures set in the jaws and used for biting and chewing
senses.definitionCN: 嵌在上颌与下颌中的坚硬钙化结构，用于咬与咀嚼
senses.example: The dentist found a small crack in the back tooth.
senses.exampleCN: 牙医在后面一颗牙上发现了一条小裂缝。
senses.why: The word is inherited from Old English toth, with a Germanic plural that changes the vowel to teeth.
senses.whyCN: 这个词继承自古英语 toth，其日耳曼语的复数通过元音变化成 teeth。

senses.title: A pointed part of a tool
senses.definition: a projecting part on a comb, a saw, a gear, or a zip
senses.definitionCN: 梳子、锯、齿轮或拉链上凸出的部件
senses.example: One tooth of the zip was bent out of line.
senses.exampleCN: 拉链上有一个齿歪出了线。
senses.why: A comb or a saw works exactly as the mouth does, gripping or cutting with small hard points, so the same word serves.
senses.whyCN: 梳子或锯的工作方式与嘴相同，都是用小而硬的尖端去抓或切，于是同一个词就沿用了。

senses.title: A liking for a kind of food
senses.definition: in informal speech, a liking for a particular kind of food or activity
senses.definitionCN: 口语中表示对某种食物或活动的偏好
senses.example: She has a sweet tooth and never refuses pudding.
senses.exampleCN: 她爱吃甜食，从不拒绝布丁。
senses.why: A craving feels like something in the mouth that wants to bite, so the phrase gives appetite a tooth of its own.
senses.whyCN: 馋意就像嘴里有个想咬东西的部件，于是这个说法也给食欲安上了一颗牙。

senses.title: A tooth in phrases of retaliation
senses.definition: used in the old legal phrase an eye for an eye and a tooth for a tooth
senses.definitionCN: 用于「以眼还眼、以牙还牙」这一古老法律短语中
senses.example: The old code demanded a tooth for a tooth, but the new one asks for payment.
senses.exampleCN: 旧律条要求以牙还牙，新法典只要求赔偿。
senses.why: The law of equal revenge names the injured part itself, so losing a tooth is repaid by a tooth.
senses.whyCN: 对等报复的律条直接点出受伤的部位，所以失去一颗牙就以一颗牙偿还。

senses.title: The hard surface that does work
senses.definition: the part of something that grips, cuts, or bites down
senses.definitionCN: 某物中起抓握、切割或咬合作用的部位
senses.example: The clamp has worn teeth that no longer hold the pipe.
senses.exampleCN: 夹具的齿磨平了，再也夹不住管子。
senses.why: The point that bites down is the part that does the work, so the word spreads to any gripping surface.
senses.whyCN: 真正用力的是那个咬下去的点，于是这个词扩展到任何起抓握作用的面。

senses.title: Age shown by the teeth
senses.definition: used in phrases that judge age from the state of the teeth, as with horses
senses.definitionCN: 用于按牙齿状况判断年龄的短语，如对马
senses.example: Judging by the tooth, the horse is older than the seller says.
senses.exampleCN: 从牙齿看，这匹马比卖主说的年纪大。
senses.why: Teeth wear in a fixed order, so a farmer reads age in them the way one reads a calendar.
senses.whyCN: 牙齿按固定次序磨损，农人看牙如同看日历一样读出年龄。

senses.title: A child growing a tooth
senses.definition: the emergence of a first tooth in a baby
senses.definitionCN: 婴儿第一颗牙长出
senses.example: The baby cut her first tooth at seven months and chewed everything after that.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子七个月时出了第一颗牙，此后什么都想咬。
senses.why: The first tooth is the child's first tool, so cutting it marks the start of eating solid food.
senses.whyCN: 第一颗牙是孩子拥有的第一件工具，它长出来便标志着开始吃固体食物。

senses.title: The unpleasantness of a task
senses.definition: used in the phrase get one's teeth into to mean dealing with hard work properly
senses.definitionCN: 用于 get one's teeth into，表示认真对付难事
senses.example: The new project finally gave her something to get her teeth into.
senses.exampleCN: 这个新项目终于让她有了一件可以狠下功夫的事。
senses.why: Hard work is treated as food that needs biting, so sinking the teeth in means committing fully.
senses.whyCN: 难事被当作需要咬住的食物，所以把牙扎进去就是全力投入。

intro.en: Tooth is one of the oldest words in English, from Old English toth, with relatives in every Germanic language and a very old Indo-European root behind them.
intro.cn: tooth 是英语最古老的词之一，来自古英语 toth，在所有日耳曼语中都有亲属词，其背后还有一个非常古老的印欧词根。

items.en: Toth names the biting organ, and the plural tech changes the vowel, a pattern still kept in teeth.
items.cn: 古英语 toth 指咬噬器官，复数 tech 通过元音变化构成，这一模式至今保存在 teeth 里。

items.en: Old Norse tenn, Old High German zan, and Gothic tunthus all trace back to one Germanic stem.
items.cn: 古诺斯语 tenn、古高地德语 zan 与哥特语 tunthus 都可上溯到同一个日耳曼语词干。

items.en: The Latin dens and the Greek odous belong to the same very old Indo-European family.
items.cn: 拉丁语 dens 与希腊语 odous 属于同一个非常古老的印欧语族。

items.en: The spelling moves through toth and tothe, and the modern form loses the final vowel sound.
items.cn: 拼写经历 toth 与 tothe 等形态，现代形式丢掉了末尾的元音。

items.en: The word extends early to pointed parts of tools, since a saw tooth bites wood as a tooth bites bread.
items.cn: 这个词很早扩展到工具的尖齿，因为锯齿咬木头正如牙齿咬面包。

items.en: Expressions like sweet tooth and a tooth for a tooth fix the word in proverb and in idiom.
items.cn: sweet tooth 与 a tooth for a tooth 这类说法把这个词固定在谚语与习语里。

note.en: The look-alike group collects compounds and derivatives built on the word, while the near-meaning group gathers the parts and products of the mouth.
note.cn: 形近组收集由本词构成的复合词与派生词，近义组则汇集口腔部位及相关物。

without teeth, or without real power
pain in a tooth
a small enclosed space or stall
entries.definitionCN: 小间；摊位，只是拼写相近，词源不同

entries.definition: the firm pink flesh around the teeth
either of the two bones that hold the teeth

normalIntro.en: These memories use the irregular plural, the compounds with ache and brush, and the tool sense that grew from biting.
normalIntro.cn: 下面几条利用不规则复数、与 ache 和 brush 等构成的搭配，以及由「咬」生长出的工具义。

normal.en: The plural is teeth, not tooths, and the vowel change is the same one in foot and feet.
normal.cn: 复数是 teeth 而不是 tooths，这个元音变化与 foot 变 feet 相同。

normal.en: Toothache adds ache to tooth, and the compound is written as one word.
normal.cn: toothache 由 tooth 加 ache，写成一体。

normal.en: A sweet tooth is an appetite for sugar, and the phrase treats the liking as a body part.
normal.cn: a sweet tooth 指爱吃甜食，这个说法把偏好当作一个身体部件。

normal.en: A tooth for a tooth is the oldest legal formula the word appears in.
normal.cn: a tooth for a tooth 是这个词出现的最古老法律套语。

normal.en: A saw has teeth because it bites wood, which is why tools borrow the word.
normal.cn: 锯有齿是因为它咬木头，工具正是因此借用了这个词。

abstract.en: Picture a hard white ridge flashing behind a laugh and then gone.
abstract.cn: 想象笑时露出一道坚白的棱，随即又消失。

abstract.en: Think of gears meshing, each ridge falling into the gap of the next wheel.
abstract.cn: 想齿轮咬合，每个齿落进另一个轮的凹槽。

abstract.en: A tooth is the only part of the body you see being used as a tool every day.
abstract.cn: 牙齿是身体里唯一每天当工具用的部件。

examples.en: The child lost a front tooth and laughed at the gap.
examples.cn: 孩子掉了一颗门牙，对着那个缺口笑。

examples.en: Two teeth on the large gear are worn away.
examples.cn: 大齿轮上有两个齿已经磨损。

examples.en: He has a sweet tooth and keeps chocolate in his desk.
examples.cn: 他爱吃甜食，抽屉里总放着巧克力。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「凸」——牙是嘴里最硬、最凸出的那一排。

root: 古英语 toth（复数 tech）→ 现代 tooth（复数 teeth）。日耳曼语同源词有古诺斯语 tenn、古高地德语 zan；更远处与拉丁语 dens、希腊语 odous 同族。

sensesIntro.en: The entry begins with the biting organ, follows the same shape into combs, saws, and gears, and then collects the idioms in which a tooth stands for appetite, for revenge, and for age.
sensesIntro.cn: 条目从咬噬器官写起，再顺着同一形状走入梳、锯与齿轮，然后汇集那些用「牙」表示食欲、报复与年龄的习语。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hard white ridge made for biting.
core.cn: 核心意象：一排为咬合而生的坚硬白棱。

branches.en: The tooth itself and the cutting of a first tooth.
branches.cn: 牙齿本身与第一颗牙的长出。

definition_zh: 结果；成绩；导致
definition_en: something that happens because of an action, event or process
core_image: 石子落入水中，一圈圈波纹向外扩散开来
scene: 连续熬夜之后，他在体检中得到了一个令人担忧的结果。 After several late nights, he received a worrying result in his medical check.
sceneCN: 这里 result 是「结果」（第 1 个义项：某个过程或行动带来的结局）；句意：连续熬夜之后，他在体检中得到了一个令人担忧的结果。

senses.title: An outcome
senses.definition: something that happens because of something else
senses.definitionCN: 因其他事物而发生的结果
senses.example: The accident was the result of careless driving.
senses.exampleCN: 这场事故是粗心驾驶的结果。
senses.why: The Latin source means to spring back, and an outcome springs from its cause.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语来源意为弹回，而结果正是从原因中弹出来的。

senses.title: A score or grade
senses.definition: the score or mark achieved in a test or competition
senses.definitionCN: 在考试或比赛中取得的分数或名次
senses.example: Her exam results were the best in the class.
senses.exampleCN: 她的考试成绩是班里最好的。
senses.why: A score is the measured outcome of effort in a test.
senses.whyCN: 分数就是考试努力被测量出来的结果。

senses.title: To cause something
senses.definition: to happen as a consequence, usually with in or from
senses.definitionCN: 作为后果而发生，通常与 in 或 from 连用
senses.example: The delay resulted in a missed flight.
senses.exampleCN: 这次延误导致错过了航班。
senses.why: As a verb, the word points from a cause to whatever it brings about.
senses.whyCN: 作动词时，这个词从原因指向它所带来的一切。

intro.en: Result comes from Latin resultare, to spring back, through French resulter.
intro.cn: result 经法语 resulter 源自拉丁语 resultare（弹回）。

items.en: Saltare means to leap.
items.cn: saltare 意为跳跃。

items.en: Resultare means to spring back.
items.cn: resultare 意为弹回。

items.en: Resulter carries the sense of following from something.
items.cn: resulter 带有「由某事物而来」的含义。

items.en: Result names the outcome that follows a cause.
items.cn: result 指随原因而来的结果。

items.en: The verb result in marks a consequence.
items.cn: 动词短语 result in 标记一种后果。

note.en: Result is close to effect and consequence and pairs with cause.
note.cn: result 与 effect、consequence 相近，并与 cause 相对。

normalIntro.cn: result 是原因弹回来的东西，就像石子激起的涟漪。

normal.en: As a result means because of what happened.
normal.cn: as a result 意为由于所发生的事。

normal.en: Result in points forward to the effect.
normal.cn: result in 指向后来的结果。

normal.en: Result from points back to the cause.

normal.en: Exam results are measured outcomes.

normal.en: Compare outcome: a result is immediate, an outcome is the final end.
normal.cn: 对比 outcome：result 较直接，outcome 是最终结局。

abstract.en: Picture a stone dropping and rings spreading out.

abstract.en: Imagine a ball bouncing back from a wall.
abstract.cn: 想象球从墙上弹回。

abstract.en: Think of a seed that finally shows as a flower.

examples.en: The result of the vote surprised everyone.
examples.cn: 投票结果让所有人吃惊。

examples.en: She checked her results online.
examples.cn: 她在网上查询了自己的成绩。

examples.en: Heavy rain resulted in the game being canceled.

root: 拉丁语 re-（回）＋ saltare（跳）→ resultare（弹回）→ 法语 resulter → result，核心义「从原因中弹回来的结局」。

sensesIntro.en: Result first names an outcome, then a test score, and as a verb it points to what a cause brings about.
sensesIntro.cn: result 先指结果，再指考试成绩，作动词时指原因所带来的一切。

core.cn: 核心意象：石子入水后向外扩散的波纹。

branches.cn: 基本义是随原因而来的一切。

branches.en: The verb links a cause to its consequence.

definition_zh: 更喜欢；宁愿；优先考虑；提出（控告、索赔）；提拔（旧义）；按自己的判断决定
definition_en: to like one thing more than another, or to choose it rather than the alternative
core_image: 两扇门并排摆在面前，一只手已经按在右边那扇的把手上，左边的门连碰都没碰
scene: 清早的月台上，通勤者在慢车与快车之间反复比较， Many commuters prefer the slower train because it is quieter.
sceneCN: 这里 prefer 指「在两样东西中更喜欢其中一样，因而选它」（第 1 个义项：在两选项中更喜爱其一）；句意为许多通勤者更喜欢慢车，因为它更安静。图中可辨识物件：并排的两列车门、月台长椅、通勤者的手提包、站牌；对应第 1 个义项。

collocations.zh: 喜欢 A 胜过 B

senses.title: Like one thing more than another
senses.definition: to like or want one thing more than another
senses.definitionCN: 比另一件东西更喜欢或更想要某一件
senses.example: She prefers tea to coffee.
senses.exampleCN: 比起咖啡，她更喜欢茶。
senses.why: Prae- means before and ferre means to carry, so the liked thing is carried in front of the other in one's esteem.
senses.whyCN: prae- 意为「在前」，ferre 意为「搬运」，被喜欢的那样东西于是被搬到另一样东西前面，排在心上更靠前的位置。

senses.title: Choose one option rather than the other
senses.definition: to choose one course or option rather than another because it suits one better
senses.definitionCN: 因为更合心意而选择一种做法或选项，而不是另一种
senses.example: We preferred to walk rather than wait for the bus.
senses.exampleCN: 我们宁愿走路，也不想等公交。
senses.why: Once one thing is placed in front, the hand follows it, so preference turns into a choice between courses of action.
senses.whyCN: 一样东西一旦被放到前面，手就会跟着它走，于是「更喜欢」变成了在几种做法之间的选择。

senses.title: Give precedence to a claim or method
senses.titleCN: 给予某项主张或方法优先地位
senses.definition: to treat one claim, method or person as more important than the others
senses.definitionCN: 把某项主张、方法或某个人看得比其他更重
senses.example: The committee preferred the cheaper design.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会更倾向于那个造价更低的方案。
senses.why: Ranking is placing in a row, and what is carried to the front of the row is what counts first.
senses.whyCN: 排序就是把东西排成一列，被搬到最前面的那一个，就是最先被考虑的那一个。

senses.title: Bring a charge or claim before a court
senses.titleCN: 向法庭提出控告或主张
senses.definition: to bring a charge, claim or request formally before a court or an authority
senses.definitionCN: 正式向法庭或主管机关提出控告、索赔或请求
senses.example: The prosecutor preferred charges of fraud against the firm.
senses.exampleCN: 检察官对这家公司提出了欺诈指控。
senses.why: Legal Latin kept the literal sense of bringing something forward, so a charge is carried before the bench.
senses.whyCN: 法律拉丁语保留了「把东西搬到前面」的字面意思，因此控告就是被搬到法官席前的东西。

senses.title: Advance someone to a higher office
senses.titleCN: 把某人提拔到更高的职位
senses.definition: to promote someone to a higher position or a more valuable office
senses.definitionCN: 把某人提升到更高或更优厚的职位
senses.example: The bishop was preferred to a wealthier see.
senses.exampleCN: 这位主教被提拔到一个更富裕的教区。
senses.why: A person raised above his peers is literally carried in front of them in rank.
senses.whyCN: 一个人被抬到同辈之上，在位次上就是被搬到了他们前面。

senses.title: Regard one explanation as more likely
senses.titleCN: 认为某一种解释更可能成立
senses.definition: to judge one explanation, reading or hypothesis as more likely than another
senses.definitionCN: 判断某一种解释、读法或假说比另一种更可能
senses.example: Historians prefer the simpler reading of the letter.
senses.exampleCN: 历史学家更认可对这封信较为简单的解读。
senses.why: The mind also carries things forward: among competing readings, one is placed ahead of the rest.
senses.whyCN: 心思也会搬东西：在几种相互竞争的解释里，总有一种被放到其余之前。

senses.title: Express a softer wish about another person's action
senses.titleCN: 委婉表达希望对方如何做
senses.definition: to say politely that one would rather have something done in a particular way
senses.definitionCN: 礼貌地表示自己更希望某事以某种方式进行
senses.example: I would prefer it if you called before coming.
senses.exampleCN: 我希望你来之前先打个电话。
senses.why: The comparative force softens a request: the speaker names a preferred arrangement instead of giving an order.
senses.whyCN: 比较的意味让请求变软：说话人只是说出更合意的安排，而不是下命令。

senses.title: Decide at one's own discretion
senses.titleCN: 按自己的判断自行决定
senses.definition: to decide according to one's own judgment, especially in formal rules that leave the choice open
senses.definitionCN: 按自己的判断作出决定，尤用于把选择权留给当事人的正式规则
senses.example: The trustee may, as he prefers, sell the land at auction.
senses.exampleCN: 受托人可以按自己的判断，以拍卖方式出售这块土地。
senses.why: The oldest sense of placing one thing before another survives as the freedom to put whichever course one likes first.
senses.whyCN: 「把某样东西放到前面」这个最古老的意思，在这里留存为「可以把中意的做法排在前面」的自由。

intro.en: Prefer comes through Old French from Latin praeferre, built on prae- meaning before and ferre meaning to carry or bear. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: prefer 经古法语来自拉丁语 praeferre，由 prae-「在前」与 ferre「搬运、承载」构成。年代均为约数。

items.en: Ferre meant to carry or bear, and its past participle latus stands behind English words such as relate and translate. Its older source is generally reconstructed as a root meaning to carry.
items.cn: ferre 意为「搬运、承载」，其过去分词 latus 支撑着 relate、translate 等英语词。它更早的来源通常被重构为一个表示「搬运」的词根。

items.en: Prae- meaning before plus ferre produced praeferre, to place or carry in front, and by extension to value one thing above another.
items.cn: 表示「在前」的 prae- 加 ferre 构成 praeferre，意为「放到前面、搬在前面」，并引申为把某物看得比另一物更重。

items.en: Old French preferer brought the verb into English in the late fourteenth century, at first in the sense of putting a person or thing before others.
items.cn: 古法语 preferer 在十四世纪后期把这个动词带入英语，最初指把人或物放到其他之前。

items.en: By the sixteenth century the verb named esteeming one thing above another, and legal usage used it for bringing a charge or request forward.
items.cn: 到十六世纪，这个动词已指看重某物胜过另一物，法律用语则用它表示把控告或请求呈到前面。

items.en: The everyday sense of liking one thing better than another settled in ordinary speech, while the legal and church senses stayed in specialized use.
items.cn: 「更喜欢某物」这一日常义在普通口语中固定下来，而法律与教会用语里的意思则留在专门场合。

items.en: Source uncertain: the first English citation is not fixed, and the deeper Indo-European root of ferre is a reconstructed form rather than a recorded word.
items.cn: 来源不确定：英语中最早的书证年代没有定论；ferre 更深的印欧语词根属重构形式，并非有记录的真实词形。

note.en: The first group shares the Latin verb ferre but differs in prefix; the second holds words for liking and picking that are close in use. One look-alike has a different origin.
note.cn: 第一组共享拉丁动词 ferre，只是前缀不同；第二组是用法相近的「喜爱、挑选」类词。其中有一个形似词来源不同。

entries.definition: Re- meaning back plus ferre: to carry a matter back to a source, hence to direct attention or consult.
entries.definitionCN: re-「向后」加 ferre：把某事带回源头，因而指指向某处或查阅。

entries.definition: Con- meaning together plus ferre: to bring matters together, hence to consult or to bestow.
entries.definitionCN: con-「共同」加 ferre：把事情带到一处，因而指商议或授予。

entries.definition: Dis- meaning apart plus ferre: to carry things in different directions, hence to be unlike.
entries.definitionCN: dis-「分开」加 ferre：把东西带向不同方向，因而指彼此不同。

entries.definition: From Old French poroffrir, built on offrir and Latin offerre meaning to bring before; it looks like prefer but the prefix and source differ.
entries.definitionCN: 来自古法语 poroffrir，由 offrir 与拉丁语 offerre「呈到面前」构成；它与 prefer 形似，但前缀与来源都不同。

entries.definition: To treat one person or option with special approval; it stresses approval rather than a comparison between two things.
entries.definitionCN: 带着特别的认可对待某个人或某种选项；它强调认可，而不是两物之间的比较。

entries.definition: To pick one option; prefer names the leaning, choose names the act.
entries.definitionCN: 挑出一个选项；prefer 命名的是倾向，choose 命名的是动作。

entries.definition: To make a choice, often in a formal or deliberate context; it does not carry the comparative force of liking one more than another.
entries.definitionCN: 作出选择，常用于正式或慎重的场合；它不带有「比另一物更喜欢」的比较意味。

entries.definition: The everyday verb for finding something pleasant; prefer adds a comparison with something else.
entries.definitionCN: 表示觉得某物令人愉快的日常动词；prefer 则加上了与另一物的比较。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real prefix, the real root, the real family and the phrases the verb keeps.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的前缀、真实的词根、真实的同族词，以及这个动词实际常用的搭配。

normal.en: prae- meaning before plus ferre meaning carry: to carry one thing in front of another.
normal.cn: prae-「在前」加 ferre「搬运」：把一样东西搬到另一样前面。

normal.en: The family runs prefer, preference, preferable, preferably, preferential and preferment.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 prefer（更喜欢）、preference（偏好）、preferable（更可取的）、preferably（更可取地）、preferential（优先的）、preferment（提拔）。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the comparison: prefer tea to coffee, prefer to wait, strongly prefer.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出比较关系：喜欢茶胜过咖啡、宁愿等待、强烈偏好。

normal.en: The same root runs through refer, confer, differ, infer and transfer, each with its own prefix.
normal.cn: 同一词根贯穿 refer、confer、differ、infer、transfer，各自配上不同的前缀。

normal.en: Legal usage keeps the old forward motion: to prefer charges is to bring them before a court.
normal.cn: 法律用法保住旧的「向前搬」动作：提出控告就是把控告呈到法庭前。

abstract.en: Picture two doors and a hand already resting on the right handle.
abstract.cn: 想象两扇门，一只手已经按在右边那扇的把手上。

abstract.en: Picture a clerk placing one file on top of a stack.
abstract.cn: 想象一名职员把一份卷宗放到整叠文件的最上面。

abstract.en: Picture a compass needle that always settles a little east of north.
abstract.cn: 想象一枚罗盘针，每次都停在正北略偏东的位置。

examples.en: Most readers prefer the shorter edition.
examples.cn: 多数读者更喜欢篇幅较短的版本。

examples.en: She preferred to say nothing until the facts were clear.
examples.cn: 在事实清楚之前，她宁愿什么都不说。

examples.en: The court preferred charges against two officers.
examples.cn: 法庭对两名警官提出了指控。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「普瑞佛」——先把喜欢的那件捧到前面 → prefer 更喜欢、宁愿

root: 拉丁 praeferre「放到前面、看重」= prae-「在前」+ ferre「搬运、承载」；ferre 的印欧语来源通常被重构为表示「搬运」的词根。英语 prefer 经古法语进入。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one gesture: one thing is carried in front of another, and that placement is applied to taste, action, ranking, legal charges, offices, explanations, polite wishes and finally to open discretion.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个动作展开：把一样东西搬到另一样前面，这个摆放再依次用于口味、行动、排序、法律控告、职位、解释、礼貌愿望，最后用于留有余地的自行裁量。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two things offered side by side, and one is carried to the front of the hand.
core.cn: 核心意象：两样东西并排摆在面前，其中一样被搬到手上更靠前的位置。

branches.en: TASTE AND ACTION: the thing carried to the front is first liked, then taken.
branches.cn: 口味与行动：被搬到前面的东西先被喜欢，再被拿走。

branches.en: RANKING: precedence is the same placement seen as order rather than desire.
branches.cn: 排序：优先地位是同一种摆放，只是被看成次序而非喜好。

branches.en: FORMAL FORWARDING: a charge or a candidate is brought before the bench or above one's peers.
branches.cn: 正式呈交：控告或人选被带到法官席前，或被抬到同辈之上。

branches.en: READING: among explanations the mind puts one ahead of the rest.
branches.cn: 解读：在几种解释中，心思把其中一种放到其余之前。

branches.en: SOFTENED WILL: a polite wish and a formal discretion both leave the preferred course to the speaker.
branches.cn: 柔化的意愿：礼貌的愿望与正式的裁量，都把中意的做法留给说话人自己。

intro.en: Prefer can be read from a Latin prefix and a Latin verb that also build a large English family.
intro.cn: prefer 可以按一个拉丁前缀与一个拉丁动词逐段读出，这两部分还构成一大族英语词。

latinIntro.en: Latin ferre gives refer, confer, differ, infer, transfer and prefer; prae- adds the sense of being in front.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 ferre 衍生 refer、confer、differ、infer、transfer 与 prefer；prae- 加上「在前面」的意思。

items.example: The prefix also appears in predict and precede.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀也出现在 predict（预测）与 precede（在……之前）里。

items.example: Its participle latus underlies translate and relate.
items.exampleCN: 它的过去分词 latus 是 translate 与 relate 的词源基础。

items.meaning: to carry in front, hence to value more
items.exampleCN: 她更喜欢早一班的那趟车。

definition_zh: 希望；愿望；想要；祝愿；许愿
definition_en: to want something to happen, especially something you cannot control, and to express that want
core_image: 生日蛋糕上那点烛火面前，一个人闭眼低头，把愿望在心里说了一遍
scene: 蛋糕上的烛光照到脸上，他闭眼低头，把愿望在心里说了一遍才吹熄。 I wish you good luck in the exam tomorrow.
sceneCN: 这里 wish 是「希望、祝愿」（第 1 个义项：希望某事发生、尤其是自己无法掌控的事）；句意为祝你明天考试顺利。闭眼低头许愿的那一刻，就是这个词的印象。

derivatives.zh: 一厢情愿的；渴望的

senses.title: To want it to be so
senses.definition: to want something to be true or to happen, especially when you cannot make it happen
senses.definitionCN: 希望某事为真或发生，尤其在自己无法使之实现时
senses.example: I wish you good luck in the exam tomorrow.
senses.exampleCN: 祝你明天考试顺利。
senses.why: The oldest sense is simply to desire, and the word keeps a soft and slightly helpless colour.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的义项就是想，这个词保留着温和而略带无力的色彩。

senses.title: To express a hope for someone
senses.definition: to say that you hope someone will be happy, safe or successful, as in good wishes
senses.definitionCN: 说希望某人幸福、平安或成功，如 good wishes
senses.example: She wished the bride and groom a long and happy life.
senses.exampleCN: 她祝愿新郎新娘百年好合。
senses.why: Desire aimed at another person becomes a blessing, which is why the word greets and closes letters.
senses.whyCN: 指向他人的愿望成了祝福，所以这个词能用来问候与收尾信件。

senses.title: A longing in the mind
senses.definition: a strong desire for something, often secret, kept as a noun
senses.definitionCN: 对某物的强烈想望，常是秘密的，作名词使用
senses.example: The old man's last wish was to see the sea again.
senses.exampleCN: 老人最后的愿望是再见一次海。
senses.why: The noun simply names the desire that the verb performs, often before it is spoken aloud.
senses.whyCN: 名词直接命名动词所做的那份欲望，往往在说出口之前就有。

senses.title: To greet with a formula
senses.definition: used in set phrases such as wish you well, to offer a polite and warm formula
senses.definitionCN: 在 wish you well 等固定说法中，用来致以礼貌而温暖的问候
senses.example: The staff wished every guest good morning at the door.
senses.exampleCN: 员工在门口向每位客人问早安。
senses.why: Greetings in most languages are blessings, so wishing is how many conversations begin.
senses.whyCN: 多数语言里的问候都是祝福，所以祝愿是许多对话的开头。

intro.en: Wish is Old English wyscan, to desire, a native Germanic verb that also gave the noun wish, an inner want.
intro.cn: wish 是古英语 wyscan（渴望），一个本土日耳曼语动词，也产生了名词 wish，指内心的想望。

items.en: wyscan meant to long for, often in prayer, and expressed a hope rather than a plan.
items.cn: wyscan 意为渴望，常用于祈祷，表达的是希望而非计划。

items.en: The verb was strong, and its noun form named the desire itself.
items.cn: 这个动词是强变化动词，其名词形式命名欲望本身。

items.en: Spelling settled as wish, and the meaning widened to polite good wishes.
items.cn: 拼写固定为 wish，词义扩展到礼貌的祝愿。

items.en: I wish plus a past form became a fixed way to speak of an unreal state.
items.cn: I wish 加过去式成了谈论不真实状况的固定说法。

items.en: The birthday wish and the wishing well kept the fairy tale sense alive in daily life.
items.cn: 生日愿望与许愿井让童话式的义项在日常生活中存活下来。

intro.en: Coach started in a Hungarian village and rolled across Europe on four wheels.
intro.cn: coach 起源于匈牙利的一个村庄，坐着四轮车驶遍了欧洲。

items.en: The name comes from Kocs, a Hungarian village famous for its carts.
items.cn: 此词源自以制车闻名的匈牙利村庄 Kocs。

items.en: French coche carried the carriage word into western Europe.
items.cn: 法语 coche 把「车厢」一词带进西欧。

items.en: Middle English coach meant the closed carriage drawn by horses.
items.cn: 中古英语 coach 指马拉的封闭式车厢。

items.en: People who carried students to exams were joked to be coaches, and the teacher sense was born.
items.cn: 人们打趣说帮学生突击应考的人像「载客马车」，教师义由此诞生。

items.en: Later the railway used coach for carriages, and the bus age kept it for long-distance coaches.
items.cn: 后来铁路把 coach 用于车厢，巴士时代又用它指长途客车。

definition_zh: 从不；永不；绝不；（表示惊讶）不会吧
definition_en: at no time in the past or future, and also used to refuse something emphatically or to show surprise
core_image: 一条两头都被封死的时间线，任何一个时刻都走不进去
scene: 深夜的电话铃一直没响，他盯着屏幕，心里明白那个人再也不会打来了。 She never called back after that night.
sceneCN: 这里 never 是「从不、一次也没有」（第 2 个义项：在任何场合都没有发生）；句意为那一夜之后她再也没回电话。图中可辨识物件：暗着的手机屏、没有来电的空桌面。

derivatives.zh: 由 never 与 the less 组合而成，义为「尽管如此」
由 never 与 more 组合，书面语，义为「不再；永不再」
由 never 与 ending 复合，义为「没完没了的」

senses.title: At no time in the past or future
senses.definition: at no time, whether in the past or in the future
senses.definitionCN: 在过去或将来的任何一个时刻都不
senses.example: I have never been to that city.
senses.exampleCN: 我从未去过那座城市。
senses.why: The word welds an Old English negative particle onto ever, so it closes every point of the timeline at once instead of denying one event.
senses.whyCN: 这个词把古英语的否定小词焊在 ever（任何时候）上，于是一次性封住了时间线上的每一个点，而不是只否定某一件事。

senses.title: On no occasion; not once
senses.definition: not on a single occasion, even when the chance keeps coming back
senses.definitionCN: 即使机会反复出现，也一次都没有发生过
senses.example: She never misses a chance to help a neighbour.
senses.exampleCN: 她从不错过帮助邻居的机会。
senses.why: Because the negative is attached to ever rather than to one occasion, it runs through every repetition and finds none of them.
senses.whyCN: 否定词挂在「任何时候」上，而不是挂在某一次机会上，所以它把所有重复出现的场合都数了一遍，结论是一个也没有。

senses.title: Emphatic refusal or denial
senses.definition: used for a strong refusal or to say that something will certainly not happen
senses.definitionCN: 用于强烈拒绝，或表示某事肯定不会发生
senses.example: Never tell him that password.
senses.exampleCN: 绝对不要把那个密码告诉他。
senses.why: A refusal needs the heaviest word available, and a word that rules out every moment serves as a flat and final no.
senses.whyCN: 拒绝需要最有分量的词，而一个排除掉所有时刻的词，正好等于一句毫无余地的「不」。

senses.title: Surprise or disbelief
senses.definition: used alone or with a question to show that something is hard to believe
senses.definitionCN: 单独使用或跟疑问句，表示觉得某事难以置信
senses.example: Never! You cannot mean that.
senses.exampleCN: 不会吧！你不可能是那个意思。
senses.why: When a listener repeats the word on its own, the term that normally blocks time now blocks belief, and the denial turns into an exclamation.
senses.whyCN: 当听者把这个词单独喊出来时，这个平时封锁时间的词转而封锁「相信」，否定就变成了一声惊叹。

intro.en: Never is an Old English compound of a negative particle and the word for ever, and it has kept that shape for more than a thousand years.
intro.cn: never 是古英语中否定小词与「任何时候」一词的复合，这个结构保持了一千多年。

items.en: The recorded form nǣfre already meant at no time, built from ne plus ǣfre.
items.cn: 有记录的 nǣfre 已经表示「在任何时候都不」，由 ne 与 ǣfre 合成。

items.en: Ne was the general negative particle placed before another word to deny it.
items.cn: ne 是通用的否定小词，放在另一个词前面表示否定。

items.en: Āfre meant at any time and is the same word that became modern ever.
items.cn: āfre 意为「在任何时候」，也就是现代英语 ever 的前身。

items.en: Middle English spelled the word never or ner and used it for past time as well as for strong refusals.
items.cn: 中古英语把它写作 never 或 ner，既用于过去时间，也用于强烈的拒绝。

items.en: Modern English keeps the compound as one word and adds fixed phrases such as never mind and never again.
items.cn: 现代英语把这个复合词固定为一个词，并发展出 never mind、never again 等固定说法。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built on ever, the second half of never; the near-meaning group gathers words about frequency and its opposite.
note.cn: 形近组收以 ever（never 的后半部分）为核心构成的词；近义组收与频率及其反义有关的词。

entries.definition: At any time; the word that supplies the second half of never.
entries.definitionCN: 在任何时候；正是它提供了 never 的后半部分。

entries.definition: At any time that something happens; built on ever.
entries.definitionCN: 每当某事发生时；由 ever 构成。

entries.definition: In spite of that; formed from never, the and less.
entries.definitionCN: 尽管如此；由 never、the 与 less 组合而成。

entries.definition: For all future time; a literary word built on ever.
entries.definitionCN: 永远；书面语，由 ever 构成。

entries.definition: At every time; the direct opposite of never.
entries.definitionCN: 总是；每时每刻，正好是 never 的反面。

entries.definition: On only a few occasions, but not never.
entries.definitionCN: 很少；只有少数几次，但不是一次也没有。

entries.definition: Almost never, used when something happens very few times.
entries.definitionCN: 几乎从不；表示某事发生的次数极少。

entries.definition: Almost not at all, close to never in everyday speech.
entries.definitionCN: 几乎不；在日常口语里接近 never。

normalIntro.en: The word is a negative particle and ever fused together, so most of its family keeps circling the idea of no moment at all.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词由否定小词与 ever 融合而成，所以它的词族大多围绕「没有任何一个时刻」打转。

normal.en: Split never into ne plus ever: not ever, at no time.
normal.cn: 把 never 拆成 ne 加 ever：任何时候都不，也就是从不。

normal.en: The ever inside never is the same ever you use in questions such as have you ever.
normal.cn: never 里的 ever，就是你在 have you ever 这类问句里用的那个 ever。

normal.en: Since Middle English the two parts have been written as one word, unlike most other ne compounds.
normal.cn: 从中古英语起，这两部分就写成一个词，和大多数其他带 ne 的复合词不同。

normal.en: The phrase never mind uses the same word to cancel a topic rather than a moment.
normal.cn: never mind 里用的是同一个词，只是它取消的是一个话题，而不是一个时刻。

normal.en: Fixed pairs such as never again and almost never show how firmly the word locks a time span.
normal.cn: never again、almost never 这类固定组合，显示出这个词把一段时间锁得多么死。

abstract.en: A word that denies every point of time at once is stronger than a word that denies one event.
abstract.cn: 一个能同时否定时间线上每个点的词，比只否定一件事的词要强硬得多。

abstract.en: When the same word later denies belief instead of time, you can hear how easily a closed door becomes an exclamation.
abstract.cn: 当同一个词后来否定的是「相信」而不是时间，你能听出一扇关死的门多么容易变成一声惊叹。

abstract.en: Never is a reminder that some doors are not merely shut for now; they are shut on every side.
abstract.cn: never 提醒人：有些门不是暂时关上，而是四面都封死了。

examples.en: I have never seen snow fall in this city.
examples.cn: 我从未见过这座城市下雪。

examples.en: Never open that door while the alarm is on.
examples.cn: 警报开着的时候绝对不要开那扇门。

examples.en: She never misses a chance to help a neighbour.
examples.cn: 她从不错过帮助邻居的机会。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「捏我」——他捏了我一下，我记住了：这种事「从不」再犯。

root: 古英语 ne（否定）加 ǣfre（在任何时候）合成 nǣfre，意为「任何时候都不」；拉丁语中没有可靠的同源同族词。

sensesIntro.en: The core sense is no moment at all; the senses then widen from repeated occasions to flat refusal and finally to disbelief.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是「没有任何一个时刻」；义项由此从反复出现的场合，扩展到断然拒绝，最后到难以置信。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a timeline sealed at both ends so that no moment can be entered.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条两头都封死的时间线，任何一个时刻都走不进去。

branches.en: a timeline with every point crossed out
branches.cn: 整条时间线上的每个点都被划掉

branches.en: a calendar of chances without a single check mark
branches.cn: 一页机会的日历，没有一个打勾

branches.en: a hand raised flat in refusal
branches.cn: 一只平举的手表示拒绝

branches.en: a face repeating the word in shock
branches.cn: 一张震惊地重复这个词的脸

branches.en: one denial serving both past time and every repeated occasion
branches.cn: 同一个否定，既用于过去，也用于反复出现的场合

intro.en: The word is held together by an Old English negative particle, the word for ever, their fused form, and a few modern compounds.
intro.cn: 这个词由古英语否定小词、表示 ever 的词、二者融合的形式，以及几个现代复合词共同支撑。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded; the first element is an Old English negative particle, not a Latin one.
latinIntro.cn: 没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录；它的第一个成分是古英语的否定小词，而不是拉丁语的。

items.meaning: forming words such as whoever and whatever
items.meaningCN: 构成 whoever、whatever 等词的后缀

items.meaning: in spite of that, built on never
items.meaningCN: 尽管如此，由 never 加 the less 构成
items.exampleCN: 尽管如此，她仍继续前行。

definition_zh: 最近的；最新的；近代的
definition_en: happening or existing a short time ago; fresh and up to date; belonging to modern times
core_image: 日历上刚翻过的一页，墨迹还新
scene: 报纸头版印着前一天发生的事，纸边还带着油墨味。 Recent research suggests that sleep affects memory.
sceneCN: 这里 recent 是「最近的」（第 1 个义项：不久前发生的）；句意为近期研究表明睡眠会影响记忆。画面里可留意：刚翻过的日历、带油墨味的报纸。

derivatives.zh: 最近；近来
新近；近期
新近

senses.title: Happening a short time ago
senses.definition: happening or existing only a short time before the present
senses.definitionCN: 在当下之前不久发生或存在的
senses.example: Recent research suggests that sleep affects memory.
senses.exampleCN: 近期研究表明睡眠会影响记忆。
senses.why: Latin recens meant fresh or just made, and English kept the sense of something still close in time.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 recens 意为新鲜的、刚做成的，英语保留了「在时间上仍然靠近」的含义。

senses.title: Fresh and up to date
senses.definition: containing the newest information and not yet replaced
senses.definitionCN: 包含最新信息、尚未被取代的
senses.example: The library keeps recent issues of the journal.
senses.exampleCN: 图书馆保留了这份期刊最新的几期。
senses.why: What is fresh is also current, so the word came to describe information that has not been overtaken.
senses.whyCN: 新鲜的东西也是当下的，于是这个词用来形容尚未被超越的信息。

senses.title: Belonging to modern times
senses.definition: of a period close to the present, especially in history or geology
senses.definitionCN: 属于靠近当下的时期，尤其用于历史或地质分期
senses.example: Recent history covers the last two centuries.
senses.exampleCN: 近代史涵盖过去两个世纪。
senses.why: From a few days ago the word widened to a whole historical period that is close to the present.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从「几天前」扩展到整个靠近当下的历史时期。

intro.en: Recent comes straight from a Latin adjective of freshness, and its sense widened from fresh things to fresh time and fresh periods.
intro.cn: recent 直接来自拉丁语表「新鲜」的形容词，其含义从新鲜之物扩展到新鲜的时间与时期。

items.en: Recens meant fresh, new, or just made, said of things still new to the senses.
items.cn: recens 意为新鲜的、新的、刚做成的，用于感官上仍新的事物。

items.en: The comparative recentior meant more recent, the form behind the English degree forms.
items.cn: 比较级 recentior 意为「更近期的」，是英语比较形式的来源。

items.en: Old French recent brought the adjective into English unchanged in sense.
items.cn: 古法语 recent 把这个形容词原样带入英语，含义未变。

items.en: Middle English recent applied the word to events and to writing.
items.cn: 中古英语 recent 把这个词用于事件与文字。

items.en: Modern English extended recent to news, research, and whole historical periods.
items.cn: 现代英语把 recent 扩展到新闻、研究以及整个历史时期。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers adjectives close in sound; the near-meaning group gathers words for newness and currency.
note.cn: 形近组收读音相近的形容词；近义组收表新鲜与当下的词。

entries.definition: To feel bitter about something.
Acceptable and proper.
One who rules in another's place.
Recently made or begun.
Newly arrived or newly made.
The most recent of a series.
Of the present or near past.

normalIntro.en: The word pictures something still warm from happening, like a page just turned.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词描绘刚刚发生、还带着热度的事物，像刚翻过的一页日历。

normal.en: Recent sounds like re-sent, as if news was just sent to you.
normal.cn: recent 听起来像 re-sent，仿佛消息刚刚发给你。

normal.en: In recent years is the standard phrase for the near past.
normal.cn: in recent years 是表达「近年来」的标准搭配。

normal.en: Recent research means work published not long ago.
normal.cn: recent research 指不久前发表的研究。

normal.en: The comparison uses more recent, not recenter.
normal.cn: 比较级用 more recent，而不是 recenter。

normal.en: Recent history is a period; a recent event is a moment.
normal.cn: recent history 是一段时期，a recent event 是一个瞬间。

abstract.en: The recent is the edge of time, where memory has not yet become history.
abstract.cn: 「最近的」是时间的边缘，记忆尚未变成历史。

abstract.en: What is recent feels important precisely because it is still warm.
abstract.cn: 刚发生的事显得重要，正因为它还带着温度。

abstract.en: Every age calls its own news recent and the rest old.
abstract.cn: 每个时代都把自己的新闻称为「最近的」，把其余称为旧的。

examples.en: Recent research suggests that sleep affects memory.
examples.cn: 近期研究表明睡眠会影响记忆。

examples.en: The library keeps recent issues of the journal.
examples.cn: 图书馆保留了这份期刊最新的几期。

examples.en: Recent history covers the last two centuries.
examples.cn: 近代史涵盖过去两个世纪。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 recent 联想成「日历刚翻过去的一页」：墨迹还新，就是最近的。

root: 拉丁 recens（新鲜的、刚出现的）→ 古法语 recent → 中古英语 recent → 英语 recent；同族有 recently、recency、recentness。

sensesIntro.en: The core is freshness in time; the senses move from a recent event to current information and to a modern period.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「时间上的新鲜」；义项从刚发生的事，到当下的信息，再到近代时期。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a calendar page just turned, the ink still fresh.
core.cn: 核心意象：日历刚翻过的一页，墨迹还新。

branches.en: a newspaper from yesterday
branches.cn: 昨天的报纸

branches.en: a journal issue on the shelf
branches.cn: 架子上最新一期期刊

branches.en: a chapter on the last two centuries
branches.cn: 讲述过去两个世纪的一章

branches.en: a recent event and recent data
branches.cn: 刚发生的事与最新的数据

branches.en: fresh news and modern history
branches.cn: 新鲜的新闻与近代的历史

intro.en: A short Latin adjective of freshness gives the base, and English endings produce the adverb and the nouns.
intro.cn: 一个表新鲜的简短拉丁形容词提供词根，英语词尾则造出副词与名词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base is recens, with the comparative recentior behind the English degree forms.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词根是 recens，其比较级 recentior 是英语比较形式的来源。

definition_zh: 表演；演出；执行；做；表现；履行
definition_en: to present a play, piece of music or dance to an audience; to carry out a task or operation; to work in a particular way as judged by results
core_image: 聚光灯下的舞台，演员从侧幕走出，把练过无数遍的动作一次做完
scene: 剧院的后台挤满人，化妆镜前的灯泡亮着，开场铃已经响过。 The whole cast performed without a single missed cue.
sceneCN: 这里 perform 是「表演、演出」（第 1 个义项）；句意为整台演员演下来，没有漏掉任何一个提示点。

derivatives.zh: 由 perform 加名词后缀 -ance 构成，义为「表演；表现；性能」
由 perform 加表示人的后缀 -er 构成，义为「表演者」
由 perform 加 -ing 构成，义为「表演的」，如表演艺术

senses.title: To act before an audience
senses.definition: to present a play, concert, dance or other show to people who are watching
senses.definitionCN: 把戏剧、音乐会、舞蹈等演给观众看
senses.example: The band performed three new songs.
senses.exampleCN: 乐队演唱了三首新歌。
senses.why: The French source meant to carry something through to the end, so a show that is carried through in front of an audience is exactly what the word describes.
senses.whyCN: 法语来源意为「把一件事做到底」，于是一场在观众面前从头做到尾的演出，正好就是这个词所描述的。

senses.title: To carry out a task
senses.definition: to do a task, action or operation, especially one that needs skill or care
senses.definitionCN: 做一项任务、行动或手术，尤指需要技巧或细心的
senses.example: Surgeons performed the operation in under two hours.
senses.exampleCN: 外科医生在不到两小时内完成了手术。
senses.why: The French source is about finishing a piece of business, and a task or an operation is exactly such a piece of work: it exists only to be carried through.
senses.whyCN: 法语来源说的是把一桩事务做完，而一项任务或一台手术正是这样的活儿：它存在就是为了被做完。

senses.title: To show how well you work
senses.definition: to work or function in a particular way, as judged by the results produced
senses.definitionCN: 按产生的成果来评判，以某种方式工作或运转
senses.example: The team performed well under pressure.
senses.exampleCN: 这支队伍在压力下表现出色。
senses.why: Once the verb means carrying work through, it can also describe how that carrying went, so the results become part of the meaning.
senses.whyCN: 一旦这个词表示把活儿做到底，它也能描述做得怎么样，于是成绩本身就成了一层词义。

senses.title: To fulfil a duty or promise
senses.definition: to do what you have promised to do or what your position requires
senses.definitionCN: 去做你承诺过的事，或你的职位要求你做的事
senses.example: The company failed to perform its duties under the contract.
senses.exampleCN: 公司未能履行合同规定的义务。
senses.why: A duty is the clearest case of something that exists only in order to be done, so the oldest sense of completing an obligation survives here almost unchanged.
senses.whyCN: 职责最能说明「存在就是为了被完成」的东西，所以「完成义务」这一最老的意思几乎原样留了下来。

intro.en: The usual account takes perform from Old French parfournir, to supply completely, with the intensifying par- related to Latin per-.
intro.cn: 一般认为 perform 来自古法语 parfournir（彻底提供），其中加强语气的 par- 与拉丁语 per- 有关。

items.en: The French verb fournir meant to supply or provide, and it supplies the second half of the English word.
items.cn: 法语动词 fournir 意为供给、提供，构成了这个词的后半截。

items.en: Parfournir added an intensifying par- and meant to complete or carry out fully; this is the source usually given for the English verb.
items.cn: parfournir 加上表彻底的 par-，意为完成、彻底履行；这通常被认为是英语动词的来源。

items.en: Anglo-Norman records used the verb for completing a task, an obligation or a piece of business.
items.cn: 盎格鲁—诺曼时期的文书记用这个动词，指完成一项任务、义务或一桩事务。

items.en: Middle English extended it from finishing a duty to presenting a play, since both are carried through to the end.
items.cn: 中古英语把它从「完成义务」扩展到「上演戏剧」，因为两者都要一直做到结尾。

items.en: Modern English keeps the three main uses side by side: a show on stage, a task in hand, and a level of results.
items.cn: 现代英语把三条主要用法并列保留：舞台上的演出、手上的任务，以及成绩的高低。

note.en: The look-alike group collects the noun and adjective branches of the same verb; the near-meaning group collects verbs of carrying something out.
note.cn: 形近组收同一动词的名词与形容词分支；近义组收表示「把事做出来」的动词。

entries.definition: The act of performing, or how well someone or something works.
entries.definitionCN: 表演这一行为，或某人某物运转得好不好。

entries.definition: A person who performs for an audience.
The adjective used in phrases such as performing arts.
entries.definitionCN: 用于表演艺术这类短语的形容词。

entries.definition: To do something, or to play a role on stage.
entries.definitionCN: 做某事，或在舞台上扮演角色。

entries.definition: To carry out a plan, order or difficult movement with skill.
entries.definitionCN: 有技巧地执行计划、命令或高难动作。

entries.definition: To organize and carry out an activity such as a study or a ceremony.
entries.definitionCN: 组织并实施研究、仪式之类的活动。

entries.definition: To arrange and present a play or event for an audience.
entries.definitionCN: 为观众安排并上演戏剧或活动。

normalIntro.en: The French source says supply completely, so the word keeps returning to the idea of delivering a whole thing, whether a song, an operation or a duty.
normalIntro.cn: 法语来源意为「彻底提供」，所以这个词反复回到「把整件事交付出来」这个意思，无论是一首歌、一台手术还是一份职责。

normal.en: The French source means to provide fully, so perform is about delivering the whole thing rather than a part of it.
normal.cn: 法语来源意为「完整地提供」，所以 perform 讲的是把整件事交付出来，而不是只做一部分。

normal.en: Performance adds -ance, the ending that turns a verb of doing into the doing itself.
normal.cn: performance 加 -ance，这个词尾把「做」的动词变成「做」这件事本身。

normal.en: Performer adds -er, and the result is the person who delivers the thing.
normal.cn: performer 加 -er，得到的就是那个把东西交付出来的人。

normal.en: A play is performed, an operation is performed and a duty is performed: the same verb covers all three because each is carried through.
normal.cn: 戏可以 perform，手术可以 perform，职责也可以 perform：同一个动词能管三件事，因为都要做到底。

normal.en: Perform well asks about results, perform live asks about an audience, so what follows the verb decides which sense is active.
normal.cn: perform well 问的是成绩，perform live 说的是有没有观众，所以动词后面接什么决定了哪一层意思在起作用。

abstract.en: A cue sheet backstage and a checklist in an operating room share one word, because both list steps that must be carried out in order.
abstract.cn: 后台的提示单与手术室里的核对表共用一个词，因为两者列的都是必须按顺序做完的步骤。

abstract.en: The word treats a concert, an operation and a promise as the same shape: something begun, done and finished in front of others.
abstract.cn: 这个词把音乐会、手术和承诺看成同一个形状：开始、做完，并在别人面前收尾。

abstract.en: When we say a machine performs, we quietly compare it to a performer judged by the audience.
abstract.cn: 当我们说一台机器 perform 时，其实是在悄悄把它比作一个被观众评判的表演者。

examples.en: The band performed three new songs.
examples.cn: 乐队演唱了三首新歌。

examples.en: Surgeons performed the operation in under two hours.
examples.cn: 外科医生在不到两小时内完成了手术。

examples.en: The team performed well under pressure.
examples.cn: 这支队伍在压力下表现出色。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「颇费劲」——台上看着轻松，台下颇费劲；perform 是表演，也是把事做完。

root: 一般认为来自古法语 parfournir（彻底提供、完成）：par- 与拉丁语 per-（彻底）同源，fournir 意为提供。

sensesIntro.en: The core sense is carrying something through to the end; a show, a task, a set of results and a duty are four places where that completion becomes visible.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是「把一件事一直做到结尾」；演出、任务、成绩与职责，是这种「做完」显现出来的四个场合。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an actor stepping out of the wings under a spotlight and finishing a routine rehearsed a hundred times.
core.cn: 核心意象：聚光灯下，演员从侧幕走出，把练过上百遍的动作一次做完。

branches.en: a curtain rising on a full house
branches.cn: 满座剧场里升起的幕布

branches.en: a checklist ticked off step by step
branches.cn: 一项项打勾的核对表

branches.en: a scoreboard read after the final whistle
branches.cn: 终场哨响后被人查看的记分牌

branches.en: a signed contract laid on a desk
branches.cn: 摊在桌上的一份签字合同

branches.en: a review that judges both the show and the skill
branches.cn: 同时评判演出与技艺的评论

intro.en: An Old French verb of supplying, an intensifying prefix and three English endings carry the word from an act to a person, a result and a field of art.
intro.cn: 一个表「供给」的古法语动词、一个加强前缀以及三个英语词尾，把这个词从行为带到人、结果与艺术领域。

latinIntro.en: Only the prefix is Latin: par- traces back to per-. The French verb fournir has no Latin original, which is why the Latin list stays short.
latinIntro.cn: 只有前缀是拉丁成分：par- 可上溯到 per-。法语动词 fournir 没有拉丁原型，所以拉丁同源词列得很短。

definition_zh: 价格；代价；给…定价；报价
definition_en: the amount of money for which something is sold, or what must be given up to obtain something
core_image: 货架上一枚小小的价签，数字不大，却决定了谁会拿起这件商品
scene: 货架前，顾客翻过价签看背面，又把商品放回原位，转身走向更便宜的一排。 The price of the coat was reduced twice before it sold.
sceneCN: 这里 price 指「商品的售价」（第 1 个义项：出售商品所要求的金额）；句意为这件外套的价格降了两次才卖出去。图中可辨识物件：货架价签、翻看标签的顾客、更便宜的一排商品、被放回的外套；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 给…定价；标价（动词重音不变）

derivatives.zh: 定价
标价的
昂贵的
无价的
定价过高
定价过低

senses.title: The money asked for a good
senses.definition: the amount of money a seller asks for an item or service
senses.definitionCN: 卖方为某件商品或服务索要的金额
senses.example: The price of the coat was reduced twice before it sold.
senses.exampleCN: 这件外套的价格降了两次才卖出去。
senses.why: the core sense is a stated amount, which is what a price tag shows.
senses.whyCN: 核心义是一个被标出的金额，也就是价签所显示的内容。

senses.title: What must be given up
senses.titleCN: 为得到某物必须付出的代价
senses.definition: the cost in effort, risk or lost alternatives of obtaining something
senses.definitionCN: 为获得某物而在努力、风险或放弃的其他选择上付出的代价
senses.example: The price of success was three years without weekends.
senses.exampleCN: 成功的代价是三年没有周末。
senses.why: the word extends from money to any scarce thing given up, because both are what one pays.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从金钱延伸到任何被放弃的稀缺之物，因为两者都是所付出的东西。

senses.title: To set a price on something
senses.definition: to decide and mark the amount to be charged for an item
senses.definitionCN: 决定并标出某项商品的收费金额
senses.example: They priced the tickets at twenty pounds.
senses.exampleCN: 他们把票价定为二十英镑。
senses.why: the verb is the noun turned into an act of assigning the amount.
senses.whyCN: 动词是名词转为「指派金额」的动作。

senses.title: The general level of prices
senses.definition: the average level of charges across an economy at a given time
senses.definitionCN: 某一时期一个经济体中收费的平均水平
senses.example: Prices rose faster than wages for a decade.
senses.exampleCN: 有十年时间，物价涨得比工资快。
senses.why: in the plural the word often means the general level rather than one tag.
senses.whyCN: 用复数时，这个词常指总体水平，而非一张价签。

senses.title: A reward offered for a capture
senses.titleCN: 为缉拿或寻回而设的赏金
senses.definition: a sum offered to anyone who finds a person or thing
senses.definitionCN: 向找到某人或某物者提供的金额
senses.example: A price was put on the fugitive's head.
senses.exampleCN: 有人为这名逃犯的人头设了赏金。
senses.why: the older sense treats a reward as the amount paid for a result.
senses.whyCN: 较旧的义项把赏金看作「为某个结果所付的金额」。

senses.title: A quoted buying or selling rate
senses.definition: the rate at which a dealer will buy or sell in a financial market
senses.definitionCN: 交易商在金融市场愿意买进或卖出的价位
senses.example: The bond price fell after the announcement.
senses.exampleCN: 公告之后债券价格下跌。
senses.why: financial markets quote two prices, a bid and an offer, so the noun names a rate rather than a tag.
senses.whyCN: 金融市场报出买价与卖价两个价位，因此这个名词指一个比率，而非标签。

senses.title: Odds in racing or betting
senses.definition: the odds offered on a horse or outcome, expressed as a price
senses.definitionCN: 对某匹马或某个结果开出的赔率，以价位表示
senses.example: The bookmaker shortened the price on the favourite.
senses.exampleCN: 博彩商调低了热门马匹的赔率。
senses.why: betting calls odds a price because the stake buys a chance at a return.
senses.whyCN: 博彩把赔率称作 price，因为赌注买到的是一次回报机会。

senses.title: Any scale of worth
senses.titleCN: 衡量与交换的价值尺度（抽象义）
senses.definition: the measure by which a society or person values something
senses.definitionCN: 社会或个人用来衡量某物价值的尺度
senses.example: Health has no price in the ordinary market sense.
senses.exampleCN: 健康在普通市场意义上没有价格。
senses.why: the word generalizes once value itself is what is being measured, not only goods.
senses.whyCN: 当被衡量的是价值本身而非仅商品时，这个词就一般化了。

intro.en: Price comes through Old French pris from Latin pretium 'price, value, reward'. It is a doublet of prize in the sense of value, but not of prize meaning an award. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: price 经古法语 pris 上溯拉丁 pretium「价格、价值、报酬」。它与表示「价值」的 prize 是对偶词，但与表示「奖赏」的 prize 不是。年代均为约数。

items.en: Pretium covered price, value and reward, so the Latin word already contained both the commercial and the figurative seeds.
items.cn: pretium 兼指价格、价值与报酬，因此这个拉丁词已同时含商业义与比喻义的种子。

items.en: Old French pris meant the amount asked or the worth of a thing, and passed both senses to English.
items.cn: 古法语 pris 指索要的金额或某物的价值，并把这两层意思都传给英语。

items.en: English price appears in the thirteenth century; the plural came to mean the general cost of living.
items.cn: 英语 price 出现于 13 世纪；其复数后来指一般生活成本。

items.en: Prize meaning value is a variant of price; prize meaning an award came from Old French prise 'a capture', from prendre 'to take', a different root.
items.cn: 表示「价值」的 prize 是 price 的变体；表示「奖赏」的 prize 来自古法语 prise「捕获」，再上溯 prendre「拿取」，词根不同。

items.en: The figurative price of success and the betting price of a horse extend the same core: something must be paid for an outcome.
items.cn: 「成功的代价」与赛马的「赔率」都延伸同一核心：为了某个结果必须付出某物。

items.en: The exact first English citation is approximate. Latin pretium and Old French pris are well documented.
items.cn: 最早的英语书证年代只是约数。拉丁 pretium 与古法语 pris 都有充分书证。

note.en: Group one holds words that look like price or share its root but differ in sense; group two holds near terms for an amount charged.
note.cn: 第一组是形似 price 或与其同根、但意义不同的词；第二组是表示「所收金额」的近义词。

entries.definition: As value, it is a doublet of price; as an award, it descends from prendre 'to take'. Only the first sense is etymologically the same word.
entries.definitionCN: 作「价值」解时，它是 price 的对偶词；作「奖赏」解时，上溯 prendre「拿取」。只有前一义在词源上是同一个词。

entries.definition: From Latin pretiosus 'costly', built on pretium; it describes worth, not the amount charged.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 pretiosus「贵重」，建于 pretium 之上；它描述价值，而非所收金额。

entries.definition: From ad- plus pretiare 'to value'; it means to estimate worth, not to set a selling price.
entries.definitionCN: 来自 ad- 加 pretiare「估价」；意为估算价值，而非设定售价。

entries.definition: Built on price with -y, meaning expensive; it describes the level, not the amount itself.
entries.definitionCN: 由 price 加 -y 构成，意为昂贵；它描述水平，而非金额本身。

entries.definition: The expense of making or obtaining something; price is what the buyer pays, and the two need not be equal.
entries.definitionCN: 制作或取得某物的支出；price 是买主所付，两者不必相等。

entries.definition: The amount a provider demands for a service; it is close to price but more common for services and fees.
entries.definitionCN: 服务提供者索要的金额；与 price 接近，但更常用于服务与费用。

entries.definition: A fixed payment for a professional service or privilege; it is a kind of price with a narrower setting.
entries.definitionCN: 为专业服务或特权支付的固定款项；它是范围更窄的一类价格。

entries.definition: The worth of something to a person; price is what is asked, while value is what is judged.
entries.definitionCN: 某物对某人的价值；price 是所要之数，value 是被判断的价值。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Latin pretium 'value': the same root runs through price, precious and appraise.
normal.cn: 拉丁 pretium「价值」：同一词根贯穿 price、precious 与 appraise。

normal.en: The family runs price, pricing, priced, pricey, priceless, overprice, underprice.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 price、pricing、priced、pricey、priceless、overprice、underprice。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the commercial sense: market price, price tag, price increase.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出商业义：市场价格、价签、价格上涨。

normal.en: The figurative sense is marked by of: the price of success, the price of silence.
normal.cn: 比喻义由 of 标出：成功的代价、沉默的代价。

normal.en: Betting uses price for odds, because a stake buys a chance at a return.
normal.cn: 博彩用 price 指赔率，因为赌注买到的是一次回报机会。

abstract.en: Picture a tiny tag that decides whether a hand reaches out or moves on.
abstract.cn: 想象一枚小小的价签，决定一只手是伸出去还是走开。

abstract.en: Picture a coin placed on one side of a scale and a thing on the other.
abstract.cn: 想象天平一边放硬币，另一边放物品。

abstract.en: Picture a finish line with a toll booth in front of it.
abstract.cn: 想象一条终点线前面立着一个收费亭。

examples.en: The price of the ticket includes the ferry crossing.
examples.cn: 票价包含渡船费用。

examples.en: They paid a high price for ignoring the warning.
examples.cn: 他们因忽视警告付出了高昂代价。

examples.en: The dealer quoted a price for the old car.
examples.cn: 经销商为这辆旧车报了价。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「price（价格）」——货架上那个决定买不买的数字 → 价格、代价

root: 拉丁 pretium「价格、价值、报酬」→ 古法语 pris → 英语 price；与表示「奖赏」的 prize 不同源，但与表示「价值」的 prize 属对偶词。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one number: a seller states what a thing costs, and that number is then read as a tag, a sacrifice, a verb, a general level, a reward, a quoted rate, betting odds, and finally any scale of worth.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个数字展开：卖方说出某物要多少钱，这个数字再被读作价签、牺牲、动词、总体水平、赏金、报价、赔率，最后是任何价值尺度。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one small tag whose number decides whether a hand reaches out.
core.cn: 核心意象：一枚小价签，其数字决定一只手是否伸出。

branches.en: AMOUNT AND ACT: the number on the tag, and the act of putting it there.
branches.cn: 金额与动作：价签上的数字，以及把数字放上去的动作。

branches.en: SACRIFICE AND SCALE: what must be given up, and the wider measure of worth it implies.
branches.cn: 牺牲与尺度：必须放弃的东西，以及它所含的更广价值尺度。

branches.en: THE GENERAL LEVEL: prices in the plural become the cost of living.
branches.cn: 总体水平：复数的 prices 成为生活成本。

branches.en: REWARD AND QUOTE: a sum offered for a capture, and a rate quoted in a market.
branches.cn: 赏金与报价：为缉拿所设的金额，以及市场中报出的价位。

branches.en: BETTING ODDS: the stake buys a chance, so the odds are called a price.
branches.cn: 博彩赔率：赌注买到机会，因此赔率被称作价格。

intro.en: Price is a borrowed Latin noun that English has turned into a verb, an adjective and an action noun, so the family spreads in several directions.
intro.cn: price 是借入的拉丁名词，英语把它变成动词、形容词与动作名词，因此词族向多个方向展开。

latinIntro.en: Latin pretium, pretiosus and pretiare supply price, precious, appraise and appreciate; English suffixes supply pricing, priced, pricey and priceless.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 pretium、pretiosus 与 pretiare 提供 price、precious、appraise 与 appreciate；英语后缀提供 pricing、priced、pricey 与 priceless。

items.example: The root carries both money and worth.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根兼含金钱与价值。

items.structure: Latin pretium via Old French pris
items.example: The price held steady all year.
The book is priced at twelve pounds.
The seats were pricey but comfortable.
The diary is priceless to historians.
items.exampleCN: 这本日记对历史学者而言无价。
卖方把这套房子定价过高。

items.example: They underpriced the tickets and sold out.
items.exampleCN: 他们把票价定得过低，结果售罄。
一位估价师为这幅画估了价。

latinEntries.meaning: to value, set a price on

definition_zh: 自豪；骄傲；傲慢；自尊（心）；狮群；以……为荣
definition_en: a warm feeling about one's own or another's achievement; an excessive sense of one's own importance; self-respect; a group of lions; and, as a verb, to feel proud about something one has
core_image: 胸膛往上一提，下巴微微抬起的那一瞬
scene: 毕业典礼上，主持人念到儿子的名字，母亲坐在观众席里，背一下子挺直了。 Her face shone with pride as her son walked across the stage to take his diploma.
sceneCN: 这里 pride 指「自豪、骄傲」（第 1 个义项：因自己或亲近的人取得成绩而心里发亮）；句意为儿子走上台领取毕业证书时，她脸上泛着自豪的光。图中可辨识物件：毕业证书、观众席、被念到名字的学生。

pos.zh: 自豪；骄傲；傲慢；自尊；狮群
以……为荣（用于 pride oneself on）

derivatives.zh: 与 pride 同属古英语 prūd 词族，但不是由 pride 加后缀得来：pride 是名词，proud 是形容词，义为「自豪的；骄傲的」
由 pride 加形容词后缀 -ful 构成，义为「自负的；傲慢的」
由形容词 proud 加 -ly 构成，义为「自豪地；得意地」，与 pride 同源而词形不同

senses.title: A warm feeling about one's own or another's success
senses.definition: a feeling of deep pleasure and satisfaction that comes from what you or people close to you have done or possess
senses.definitionCN: 因自己或亲近的人所做成、所拥有的事而感到的深切愉快与满足
senses.example: She looked at her finished painting with quiet pride.
senses.exampleCN: 她带着平静的自豪看着自己画完的画。
senses.why: The Old English noun first named the bare quality of being proud, and English kept its warmer half: the lift a person feels when something of theirs turns out well.
senses.whyCN: 古英语名词最早只指「骄傲」这种性质，英语留下了它温暖的一半：当自己这边的事情做成了，人心里往上一提，这就是自豪。

senses.title: An exaggerated belief in one's own importance
senses.definition: an unreasonable feeling that you are better or more important than other people
senses.definitionCN: 毫无道理地觉得自己比别人强、比别人重要
senses.example: It was pride, not principle, that stopped him from admitting the mistake.
senses.exampleCN: 让他不肯认错的是自大，而不是原则。
senses.why: The same self-regard that lifts a person up can also close the ears: once the good opinion of oneself grows past what the facts support, the word slides into the vice that preachers warn against.
senses.whyCN: 同一种自我看重既能让人挺起胸，也能堵住耳朵：当一个人对自己的好评超过了事实能撑住的分量，这个词就滑向传道者所警告的那种恶。

senses.title: The respect a person keeps for themselves
senses.definition: a proper sense of one's own worth that keeps a person from doing something shameful
senses.definitionCN: 对自己价值的正当意识，使人不肯做出丢脸的事
senses.example: He had too much pride to ask for help with the rent.
senses.exampleCN: 他的自尊心太强，不肯开口求人帮忙付房租。
senses.why: Between the warm sense and the arrogant one lies a third: pride as the floor a person refuses to sink below, the line kept even when nobody is watching.
senses.whyCN: 在「暖」和「傲」之间还有第三层：pride 是一个人拒绝再往下退的那块地板，即使没人看着也不肯越过的界线，所以是自尊。

senses.title: A group of lions living and hunting together
senses.definition: a group of lions that live and hunt together, usually led by related females
senses.definitionCN: 共同生活、共同捕猎的一群狮子，通常由有亲缘关系的母狮带领
senses.example: A pride of lions lay in the shade, waiting for the heat to pass.
senses.exampleCN: 一群狮子卧在树荫里，等暑气过去。
senses.why: This sense comes from medieval hunting language, where each kind of animal was given its own company name; naming a band of lions was one entry in that list, and only this one survived in everyday use.
senses.whyCN: 这个义项来自中世纪的狩猎用语，当时人们给每一种动物的群体都起一个专门的集合名，狮子那一栏就是 pride，而这一栏是唯一留到日常英语里的。

senses.title: To feel proud about a skill or possession of one's own
senses.definition: to feel a strong, often slightly self-satisfied pleasure about a skill, quality, or possession of one's own
senses.definitionCN: 对自己拥有的本领、品质或东西感到强烈的、常带点自得的满意
senses.example: The old chef prides himself on never using a shortcut.
senses.exampleCN: 这位老厨师最得意的是自己从不走捷径。
senses.why: The noun turned into a verb inside the pattern to pride oneself on, where oneself is the person being lifted and the preposition on names the thing that does the lifting.
senses.whyCN: 名词套进 to pride oneself on 这个句式后就当动词用：oneself 是被抬起来的那个自己，介词 on 后面则是抬人的理由，也就是凭什么觉得自己了不起。

intro.en: Pride is an Old English noun built on the adjective proud, and that adjective is generally traced through French to a Late Latin word for profit; the word therefore began as a judgement of worth before it split into warm and cold senses.
intro.cn: pride 是古英语里由形容词 proud 造出的名词，而那个形容词一般认为经法语上溯到晚期拉丁语中表示「有好处」的词；所以它最初是对「有没有价值」的判断，之后才分成暖、冷两路。

items.en: The Latin verb prodesse meant to be of use or of advantage, and its stem prōd- is the base that later Romance forms are usually traced to.
items.cn: 拉丁语动词 prodesse 意为「有用、有好处」，一般认为后来的罗曼语词形都追到它的词干 prōd-。

items.en: The Late Latin form prode meant useful or profitable, and in the spoken Latin of the provinces it also took on the colour of brave or worthy.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语的 prode 意为「有用的、有利的」，在各省的口语拉丁语里又沾上了「勇敢、可敬」的色彩。

items.en: Old French prud or prod described a man who was brave and worthy, a sense still visible in the modern French preux.
items.cn: 古法语 prud、prod 形容人勇敢可敬，这层意思在今天的法语 preux 里还能看到。

items.en: English borrowed the adjective as prūd, which in Old English already meant proud, arrogant, and splendid at the same time; from it the noun prȳde was formed.
items.cn: 英语借入这个形容词，写作古英语 prūd，当时就同时表示「骄傲的、傲慢的、华贵的」三面；名词 prȳde 正是由它造出来的。

items.en: Middle English prede or pride settled on the spelling pride, and the old single quality divided into praise-worthy self-respect and blame-worthy conceit, with the lion sense added from hunting vocabulary.
items.cn: 中古英语的 prede、pride 最终定为 pride 这个拼写，原本混在一起的性质分成值得称赞的自尊与该受责备的自负，狮群一义则从狩猎词汇补进来。

note.en: The look-alike group holds the adjective that pride was built from and the words closest to it in spelling; the near-meaning group holds words for self-regard, both deserved and inflated.
note.cn: 形近组收了 pride 借以构成的那个形容词及拼写最接近的几个词；近义组收表示自我看重的词，既有应得的，也有膨胀的。

entries.definitionCN: 为自己或他人的成就感到高兴的；英语正是用它造出了名词 pride。

entries.definition: Showing too high an opinion of oneself; built on the noun with the suffix -ful.
entries.definitionCN: 过于自负的；由名词加后缀 -ful 构成。

entries.definition: A person who is easily shocked by matters of the body; it comes from a French word for a modest woman, so the similarity is only in spelling.
entries.definitionCN: 对身体方面的事容易大惊小怪的人；来自法语中表示「端庄女子」的词，只是拼写相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: To push someone or something with a finger or a stick; a different word with a different origin.

normalIntro.en: The noun was grown from an adjective that English borrowed from French, so the family keeps one ancient stem but two different shapes.
normalIntro.cn: 这个名词是从英语借自法语的形容词上长出来的，所以同族词共用一个古老词干，却有两种不同词形。

normal.en: Pride is the noun and proud is the adjective: English formed prȳde from prūd, which is why the two never look alike today.
normal.cn: pride 是名词，proud 是形容词：古英语从 prūd 造出 prȳde，所以今天两者词形完全不同。

normal.en: The -ful in prideful turns the noun into an adjective, the same -ful that appears in careful and hopeful.
normal.cn: prideful 里的 -ful 把名词变成形容词，和 careful、hopeful 里的 -ful 是同一个后缀。

normal.en: Swallow one's pride is a picture of forcing something down the throat: the feeling is still there, only hidden.
normal.cn: swallow one's pride 是一幅把东西硬咽下去的画：情绪还在，只是藏起来了。

normal.en: A pride of lions follows the old hunting habit of giving every kind of animal its own collective name.
normal.cn: a pride of lions 沿用古老的狩猎习惯：给每一种动物的群体都起一个专门的集合名。

normal.en: Pride oneself on needs the reflexive pronoun because the one who boasts is also the one being lifted.
normal.cn: pride oneself on 必须带反身代词，因为夸人的和被抬高的其实是同一个。

abstract.en: One word covers a mother's lifted chin and a tyrant's closed ears, because both are the same self looking at itself.
abstract.cn: 一个词同时装着母亲抬起的下巴和暴君堵住的耳朵，因为两者都是「自我在看自己」。

abstract.en: Pride as dignity is pride turned inward and kept quiet; pride as conceit is the same force turned outward and made loud.
abstract.cn: 作为尊严的 pride 向内收着、不出声；作为自负的 pride 是同一股力向外放、喊得很响。

abstract.en: The lion sense survives as a fossil: a whole medieval habit of naming animal groups, kept alive by one entry.
abstract.cn: 狮群义像一块化石：中世纪给动物群体起名的一整套习惯，只靠这一条留了下来。

examples.en: She looked at her finished painting with quiet pride.
examples.cn: 她带着平静的自豪看着自己画完的画。

examples.en: It was pride, not principle, that stopped him from admitting the mistake.
examples.cn: 让他不肯认错的是自大，而不是原则。

examples.en: The old chef prides himself on never using a shortcut.
examples.cn: 这位老厨师最得意的是自己从不走捷径。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「扑赖德」——一股气从胸口扑上来，赖着不走，那就是 pride。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a self looking at itself with approval; the senses divide into the warm feeling, the cold excess, the line of self-respect, the lion group, and the verb of taking pride in something.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「自我满意地看着自己」；义项由此分出温暖的自豪、过头的自负、守住的尊严、狮群，以及表示「以……为荣」的动词用法。

intro.en: Instance comes from Latin instantia, a standing near or pressing presence, from instare (to stand upon). An instance is a case that stands close enough to be shown.
intro.cn: instance 来自拉丁语 instantia「近身站立、紧逼的存在」，出自 instare「立于其上」；instance 是站得够近、可以被指给你看的案例。

items.en: Latin stare meant to stand, the same root family as insist.
items.cn: 拉丁语 stare 意为站立，与 insist 同族。

items.en: in- plus stare formed instare: to stand upon, press near.
items.cn: in- 加 stare 构成 instare：立于其上、贴近逼近。

items.en: instantia meant pressing urgency, then a present case.
items.cn: instantia 先指紧逼的紧迫，后指眼前案例。

items.en: Old French instance carried both urgency and example.
items.cn: 古法语 instance 兼指紧迫与例子。

items.en: Middle English instance settled on the example sense.
items.cn: 中古英语 instance 落定于例子义。

items.en: for instance became the classic way to lift one case out.
items.cn: for instance 成为拎出个案的经典说法。
