core_image: 地图上一枚被按下的图钉，把所有描述收束到一个点上
scene: 制片人摊开地图，用铅笔圈住河湾边的一排旧仓房。 The warehouses by the river became the location for the opening scene.
sceneCN: 这里是「外景拍摄地」（第 3 个义项：剧组在摄影棚外实拍的地方）；句意为河边那排旧仓房成了开场戏的外景地。可辨物件：地图、铅笔圈、仓房。

pos.zh: 地点；位置；定位；外景拍摄地；存储位置

derivatives.zh: 与 location 同出拉丁语 locare，义为「找出位置；安置」
由 location 加形容词后缀 -al 构成，义为「位置的；地点方面的」
由 relocate 加 -ion 构成，义为「迁移；重新安置」

senses.title: A particular place or position
senses.definition: the place where someone or something is, or where an event happens
senses.definitionCN: 某人或某物所在、或某事发生的地方
senses.example: The hotel is in a quiet location near the park.
senses.exampleCN: 这家旅馆位于公园附近一处安静的地段。
senses.why: Latin locatio named the act of placing something, and English turned that act into the place that results from it.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 locatio 指「放置」这个动作，英语由此转而指放置之后形成的那个地点。

senses.title: The act of finding where something is
senses.definition: the process of discovering or fixing the exact place of something
senses.definitionCN: 发现或确定某物确切位置的过程
senses.example: The location of the missing boat took the coast guard three days.
senses.exampleCN: 找到那条失踪小船的位置花了海岸警卫队三天。
senses.why: The noun can still name the action behind the place, so it covers the search as well as the spot finally found.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词仍能指地点背后的动作，所以既能指找到的那个点，也能指寻找这件事。

senses.title: A place used for filming outside a studio
senses.definition: a real place used for shooting a film or television scene instead of a built set
senses.definitionCN: 用来拍摄电影或电视场景的真实地点，而不是搭建的布景
senses.example: The crew spent two weeks at a mountain location.
senses.exampleCN: 摄制组在一个山区外景地待了两周。
senses.why: Film work needed a word for the real place standing in for a fictional one, and location was ready to carry that meaning.
senses.whyCN: 影视工作需要一个词来指代替代虚构场景的真实地点，location 正好承接了这个意思。

senses.title: A position in memory or on a disk
senses.definition: a place in a computer's memory or storage where a piece of data is kept
senses.definitionCN: 计算机内存或存储中保存某条数据的位置
senses.example: The program writes each record to a fixed location in memory.
senses.exampleCN: 程序把每条记录写到内存中一个固定的位置。
senses.why: Once a place can be pointed to precisely, machines borrow the word for the address where data sits.
senses.whyCN: 一旦一个地点能被精确指出，机器也用这个词来指数据所在的地址。

intro.en: Location is the Latin noun for a placing, built on the verb to place, and it reached English through French.
intro.cn: location 是拉丁语中表示「放置」的名词，建立在动词「放置」之上，经法语进入英语。

items.en: The Latin noun locus meant a place or spot and supplied the stem for the whole family.
items.cn: 拉丁语名词 locus 意为地方、地点，为整族词提供了词干。

items.en: The verb locare meant to place or set something somewhere, and it gave the action behind the noun.
items.cn: 动词 locare 意为把某物放置在某处，提供了名词背后的动作。

items.en: Locatio named a placing, and in legal Latin it could also mean a letting or a lease of property.
items.cn: locatio 指放置，在拉丁法律用语里也可指财产的出租。

items.en: Old French location carried the sense of a lease or a placing, and English borrowed the form.
items.cn: 古法语 location 带有出租或安置的意思，英语借用了这个词形。

items.en: Modern English made location the ordinary word for a place, then extended it to film sets and memory addresses.
items.cn: 现代英语让 location 成为指地点的常用词，随后扩展到影视外景与内存地址。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words on the Latin stem of placing; the near-meaning group collects nouns for a place in space.
note.cn: 形近组收同一拉丁「放置」词干上的词；近义组收表示空间位置的各类名词。

entries.definition: To find the exact place of something.
Belonging to one particular place.
A neighbourhood or a small area.
The act of moving to a different place.
entries.definitionCN: 迁往另一地点的行为；迁移。

entries.definition: A piece of ground set aside for a building or an event.
entries.definitionCN: 供建筑或活动使用的一块场地。

entries.definition: The place where something stands in relation to others.
entries.definitionCN: 某物相对于其他事物所处的位置。

entries.definition: A small area or a particular point.
entries.definitionCN: 一小块地方；某个特定地点。

entries.definition: The place where an event is held.

normalIntro.en: Location is the noun of placing: it can name the act, the resulting spot, and the special places films and computers point to.
normalIntro.cn: location 是「放置」的名词形式：它能指动作，能指由此形成的地点，也能指影视与计算机特指的位置。

normal.en: Location comes from Latin locatio, a placing, built on the verb locare.
normal.cn: location 来自拉丁语 locatio，意为放置，建立在动词 locare 之上。

normal.en: The suffix -tion turns the act of placing into the thing or result, here the place itself.
normal.cn: 后缀 -tion 把「放置」这个动作变成事物或结果，在这里就是那个地点。

normal.en: On location is a film phrase: the crew shoots where the story is supposed to happen.
normal.cn: on location 是影视用语：剧组在故事该发生的地方实拍。

normal.en: Locate is the verb, location the noun, and both keep the same Latin stem.
normal.cn: locate 是动词，location 是名词，两者共用同一拉丁词干。

normal.en: A prime location is one that everyone wants, which shows the word carries value as well as position.
normal.cn: prime location 指人人都想要的地段，说明这个词除位置之外还带着价值判断。

abstract.en: A place becomes a word only when someone needs to point at it.
abstract.cn: 一个地方只有在有人需要指认它时才变成一个词。

abstract.en: Location turns empty space into a spot with a name and a purpose.
abstract.cn: location 把空白的空间变成一个有名字、有用途的点。

abstract.en: The word travels from leases to film sets to memory chips without losing its centre.
abstract.cn: 这个词从租约走到片场，再到内存芯片，始终没有丢掉中心。

examples.en: The meeting will be held at a location outside the city centre.
examples.cn: 会议将在市中心以外的一处地点举行。

examples.en: The film was shot on location in the northern mountains.
examples.cn: 这部影片在北方山区实地拍摄。

examples.en: Please confirm the location of the server room.
examples.cn: 请确认机房的位置。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「啰个神」——地图上圈来圈去，就为找准那一个地点；记住 location 是「地点」。

root: 拉丁语 locus（地方）→ 动词 locare（放置）→ 名词 locatio（放置、出租）→ 古法语 location → 英语 location；同族词多与「地点、定位」有关。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a spot in space; the senses then split into the act of finding it, the real place a film uses, and the address data occupies.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是空间中的某个点；义项由此分出寻找它的动作、影片采用的真实地点，以及数据所占的地址。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a pin pressed into a map, gathering everything said about a place into one point.
core.cn: 核心意象：地图上一枚被按下的图钉，把关于一个地方的所有说法收束到一个点上。

branches.en: a hotel standing quietly beside a park
branches.cn: 旅馆安静地立在公园旁边

branches.en: a coast guard chart marked with a last known point
branches.cn: 海岸警卫队海图上标出的最后已知位置

branches.en: cameras and lights set up among real warehouses
branches.cn: 摄像机和灯架在真实仓房之间架起

branches.en: a record written to a numbered cell in a chip
branches.cn: 一条记录写进芯片里一个编号的格子

branches.en: a map full of pins marking chosen places
branches.cn: 一张插满图钉、标出选定地点的地图

intro.en: The word is the Latin noun of placing plus the English noun suffix -tion, so its parts all describe putting something somewhere.
intro.cn: 这个词是拉丁语「放置」的名词加上英语名词后缀 -tion，所以它的各部分都在说「把东西放到某处」。

latinIntro.en: The Latin noun locus, the verb locare and the noun locatio form one chain of placing, and English took the last link as location.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语名词 locus、动词 locare 与名词 locatio 构成一条「放置」的链，英语取最后一环为 location。

definition_zh: 相当地；还算；公正地；按规则地；（旧）完全地
definition_en: to a moderate degree, or in a just and rule-abiding manner
core_image: 一根指针停在刻度盘正中偏左：既不到顶，也不落底，读数刚好可以接受
scene: 试镜结束后评委低声交换意见，认为这位新人的表现中规中矩。 The judges agreed that the newcomer sang fairly well.
sceneCN: 这里指「相当地、还算」，对应第 1 个义项：程度适中但不夸张；句意为评委一致认为新人唱得还不错。画面要点：评委席、低声耳语、打分表。

derivatives.zh: 公平的；晴朗的（基础形容词，fairly 的词源）
公平（形容词加名词后缀，指公正的性质）
不公平的（否定前缀加基础词）
不公平地（否定前缀加副词后缀）

senses.title: To a moderate degree
senses.definition: to some extent, but not very
senses.definitionCN: 在某种程度上，但并不非常
senses.example: The film was fairly good.
senses.exampleCN: 这部电影还算不错。
senses.why: The old sense 'pleasing enough' slid from praise into moderation, and the adverb inherited that milder reading.
senses.whyCN: 旧义「还算令人满意」从称赞滑向中等，副词继承了这一较弱的读法。

senses.title: In a just manner
senses.definition: honestly and according to the rules
senses.definitionCN: 诚实地、按规则地
senses.example: Both teams played fairly.
senses.exampleCN: 两队都公平比赛。
senses.why: The adverb first walked beside the adjective: a fair deed done fairly keeps the same clean surface.
senses.whyCN: 副词最初紧随形容词：公正之事以公正之姿完成，保持同一洁净表面。

senses.title: Completely, in older use
senses.definition: used before adjectives of absolute meaning to mean quite or entirely
senses.definitionCN: 用于绝对意义形容词之前，意为相当、完全
senses.example: The old wall was fairly ruined.
senses.exampleCN: 那堵旧墙几乎完全塌了。
senses.why: Before absolute adjectives the degree reading stretches to the far end: quite, entirely.
senses.whyCN: 置于绝对形容词前时，程度义被拉到另一端：相当、完全。

intro.en: Fairly is simply the adverb of fair: the Old English adjective fair gained the Germanic adverb ending -ly, and its meaning split into 'justly' and 'moderately'.
intro.cn: fairly 就是 fair 的副词形式：古英语形容词 fair 加上日耳曼副词词尾 -ly，词义随后分裂为「公正地」与「相当地」。

items.en: Old English fæger 'beautiful, clean' already formed adverbs with endings meaning 'in a fair manner'.
items.cn: 古英语 fæger「美好、洁净」已能用副词词尾构成「以公正方式」之类的副词。

items.en: Middle English used faireliche and fairly for 'beautifully' and 'justly', both close to the adjective.
items.cn: 中古英语用 faireliche、fairly 表示「美丽地」「公正地」，都与形容词贴近。

items.en: Early Modern English kept 'justly' as the main reading in phrases like play fairly.
items.cn: 早期现代英语保留「公正地」为主要读法，如 play fairly。

items.en: In the nineteenth century the degree reading 'to a moderate extent' took over, especially before adjectives.
items.cn: 十九世纪「达到中等程度」的读法占了上风，尤用于形容词之前。

items.en: Modern English fairly before an adjective or adverb almost always softens it: fairly good, fairly quickly.
items.cn: 现代英语中 fairly 置于形容词或副词前几乎总是缓和语气：fairly good、fairly quickly。

note.en: Look-alikes share the -ly adverb ending or the fair stem; near-meaning words soften or measure degree.
note.cn: 形近组共享 -ly 副词词尾或 fair 词干；近义组用于缓和语气或度量程度。

entries.definition: the adjective fair itself; fairly is its adverb
entries.definitionCN: 形容词 fair 本身；fairly 是它的副词

entries.definition: a small magical being; sounds identical
entries.definitionCN: 小仙子；发音完全相同，词源无关

entries.definition: money paid for a journey
entries.definitionCN: 旅费；同音异义，源自「行程」一词

entries.definition: to a moderate or surprising degree
entries.definitionCN: 相当；有点（语气略强于 fairly）

entries.definition: to some degree; completely in British use
entries.definitionCN: 相当；在英国英语中可指完全

entries.definition: in a fair and right manner
entries.definitionCN: 公正地；仅覆盖公正一义

normalIntro.en: Five grips on a small adverb that both softens and judges.
normalIntro.cn: 既能缓和语气又能评判公正的小副词，五个抓手。

normal.en: fairly is fair plus -ly, so its two readings both descend from the adjective.
normal.cn: fairly＝fair+-ly，两个读法都从形容词降下来。

normal.en: Before an adjective it usually means 'quite but not very': fairly good is less than very good.
normal.cn: 置于形容词前通常表示「还算但非非常」：fairly good 弱于 very good。

normal.en: play fair and play fairly mean the same thing in sport.
normal.cn: play fair 与 play fairly 在体育里意思相同。

normal.en: rather is stronger than fairly, and quite can be stronger still in British English.
normal.cn: rather 比 fairly 语气强，英国英语里 quite 可更强。

normal.en: The fairy homophone has nothing to do with justice.
normal.cn: 同音词 fairy（仙子）与公正毫无关系。

abstract.en: Moderation is a mid-mark on a ruler: fairly points at it with a steady finger.
abstract.cn: 适中是尺子上的中点刻度：fairly 用手指稳稳点在上面。

abstract.en: A just act needs no tilt; fairly describes a beam that stays level.
abstract.cn: 公正之行无需倾斜；fairly 描述的是保持水平的横梁。

abstract.en: Softeners are the polite grammar of honesty: fairly admits a truth without shouting it.
abstract.cn: 缓和词是诚实的礼貌语法：fairly 承认真相但不喊出来。

examples.en: The instructions were fairly clear, so we finished quickly.
examples.cn: 说明还算清楚，所以我们很快做完了。

examples.en: Referees must treat both sides fairly.
examples.cn: 裁判必须公平对待双方。

examples.en: The journey took fairly long because of the snow.
examples.cn: 因为下雪，旅程花了相当长的时间。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「费尔利」——费尔（fair）之后加「利」落，公平办利索事 → 公正地、相当地。

root: fair（古英语 fæger「美好、洁净」）加日耳曼副词词尾 -ly 构成。原义「公正地、美丽地」，十九世纪起「相当地」的程度用法成为主导。

sensesIntro.en: From the adverb of fairness outward to moderate degree and old absolute use.
sensesIntro.cn: 从「公正」的副词形式扩展到中等程度义与旧的绝对用法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a needle resting at the middle of the scale, neither maxed nor empty.
core.cn: 核心意象：指针停在刻度中段，既不满格也不空格。

branches.en: THE DEGREE: quite, but not very.
branches.cn: 程度：相当，但非非常。

branches.en: THE JUSTNESS: acting without bias.
branches.cn: 公正：行事不带偏私。

branches.en: THE OLD READING: entirely, before absolute adjectives.
branches.cn: 旧读法：置于绝对形容词前表完全。

branches.en: THE BALANCE: moderation as the everyday face of fairness.
branches.cn: 平衡：中庸是公正的日常面孔。

branches.en: THE SLIDER: one adverb covering both ends of the scale.
branches.cn: 滑杆：一个副词覆盖刻度两端。

intro.en: Fairly is built with the plain Germanic adverb ending; its family is the whole fair word-tree.
intro.cn: fairly 由朴素的日耳曼副词词尾构成；词族即整个 fair 词树。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin member in this family; all forms are Germanic.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词族没有拉丁成员；所有形式都是日耳曼语。

items.example: quickly means in a quick manner
the fairness of the test was questioned
items.exampleCN: 测试的公正性受到质疑

items.example: Fair enough, you win this round.

definition_zh: 粗鲁的；无礼的；粗糙的
definition_en: not polite; offensive or insulting; roughly made or simple
core_image: 未经打磨的粗糙表面，欠缺应有的礼数
scene: 对服务员大喊大叫是很无礼的。 Shouting at the waiter is very rude.
sceneCN: 这里 rude 是「无礼的」（第 1 个义项）；句意：对服务员大喊大叫是很无礼的。

derivatives.zh: 粗鲁地
粗鲁；无礼

senses.title: Not polite
senses.definition: not polite in behavior or speech
senses.definitionCN: 言行上不礼貌的
senses.example: It is rude to interrupt.
senses.exampleCN: 打断别人说话是不礼貌的。
senses.why: The core sense is a lack of polish.
senses.whyCN: 核心义是欠缺应有的修养。

senses.title: Offensive
senses.definition: offensive or insulting in an obvious way
senses.definitionCN: 明显冒犯或侮辱人的
senses.example: He made a rude gesture.
senses.exampleCN: 他做了个粗鲁的手势。
senses.why: Impoliteness hardens into open offence.
senses.whyCN: 不礼貌固化为公开冒犯。

senses.title: Roughly made
senses.definition: roughly made or simple in a primitive way
senses.definitionCN: 制作粗糙或原始简朴的
senses.example: They sheltered in a rude wooden hut.
senses.exampleCN: 他们躲在一间简陋的木屋里。
senses.why: The old sense is raw and unformed.
senses.whyCN: 旧义是未经加工、粗糙的。

intro.en: Rude comes from Latin rudis, raw and unformed.
intro.cn: rude 源自拉丁语 rudis，意为原始、未加工的。

items.en: Rudis means raw or rough.
items.cn: rudis 意为生的、粗糙的。

items.en: Rude keeps the sense of roughness.
items.cn: rude 保留粗糙的含义。

items.en: Rude describes rough work or manners.
items.cn: rude 形容粗糙的作品或举止。

items.en: Rude shifts toward social impoliteness.
items.cn: rude 转向指社交上的不礼貌。

items.en: Rude mainly means impolite today.
items.cn: 如今 rude 主要表示不礼貌。

note.en: Rude is impolite; crude is rough or unrefined.
note.cn: rude 是不礼貌，crude 则是粗制或粗俗。

entries.definition: a statement of what is allowed
a trick
raw or roughly made
not showing good manners
causing hurt or anger
not smooth or gentle

normalIntro.en: Rude is unpolished, either in manners or in form.
normalIntro.cn: rude 是未经打磨，既指礼数也指做工。

normal.en: It is rude to point at people.
normal.cn: 用手指人是不礼貌的。

normal.en: She was rude to the driver for no reason.
normal.cn: 她无缘无故对司机无礼。

normal.en: The visitors made rude comments about the food.
normal.cn: 客人们对食物说了些粗鲁的话。

normal.en: They built a rude shelter from branches.
normal.cn: 他们用树枝搭了个简陋的棚子。

normal.en: His rude awakening came when the bill arrived.
normal.cn: 账单寄来时他才猛然醒悟。

abstract.en: Picture a rough stone never polished smooth.
abstract.cn: 想象一块从未打磨光滑的石头。

abstract.en: Imagine a door slammed in someone's face.
abstract.cn: 想象一扇门当着人的面被摔上。

abstract.en: Think of a hut made from loose branches.
abstract.cn: 想象一间用松散树枝搭成的小屋。

examples.en: The clerk was rude to every customer.
examples.cn: 那名店员对每位顾客都很无礼。

examples.en: He apologized for his rude remarks.
examples.cn: 他为自己的无礼言论道歉。

examples.en: They slept in a rude hut near the river.
examples.cn: 他们睡在河边一间简陋的木屋里。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「rude」读音像「鲁的」：言行鲁莽无礼，就是「粗鲁的」。

root: 拉丁语 rudis（生的、未加工的）经古法语进入英语，核心义「未经打磨」，由物及人引申为「无礼」。

sensesIntro.en: Rude means impolite, openly offensive, or roughly and simply made.
sensesIntro.cn: rude 意为不礼貌的、公然冒犯的，或制作粗糙简朴的。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a rough surface with no polish.
core.cn: 核心意象：没有打磨过的粗糙表面。

branches.en: The base sense is a lack of good manners.
branches.cn: 基础义是缺乏礼貌。

branches.en: Impoliteness becomes open offence.
branches.cn: 不礼貌变成公然冒犯。

branches.en: The old sense of roughness survives in objects.
branches.cn: 「粗糙」的旧义仍保留在物品上。

branches.en: Both concern behavior that harms others.
branches.cn: 两者都涉及伤害他人的行为。

branches.en: Unpolished manners and unpolished wood pair up.
branches.cn: 未修饰的举止与未打磨的木头相互对应。

intro.en: Rude comes from Latin rudis without a prefix.
intro.cn: rude 来自拉丁语 rudis，不带前缀。

latinIntro.en: Latin rudis is the direct source of rude.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 rudis 是 rude 的直接来源。

items.example: Rudis is the source of rude.
items.exampleCN: rudis 是 rude 的来源。

items.example: Rude keeps the sense of roughness.

definition_zh: 怜悯；同情；遗憾；可惜；同情（某人）
definition_en: a feeling of sorrow for the suffering of others, a cause for mild regret, or to feel sorry for someone
core_image: 雨中的长椅上，一个人把伞倾向旁边瑟缩的陌生人，自己的肩膀却湿了
scene: 冬天的车站外，一位老人蹲在湿冷的地上整理散落的行李，路过的年轻人停下脚步，弯下腰帮他捡。 She felt a sudden pity for the old man in the rain.
sceneCN: 这里是「怜悯、同情」（第 1 个义项：对他人苦难的难过与关切）；句意为她忽然对雨中的老人心生怜悯。画面里是弯腰帮忙捡行李的年轻人。

derivatives.zh: 由 pity 加 -ful 构成，义为「可怜的；令人同情的」，也可指「少得可怜的」
由 pity 加表示「没有」的后缀 -less 构成，义为「无情的；冷酷的」
由 self 与 pity 复合而成，指「自怜」

senses.title: Sympathy for another person's suffering
senses.definition: a feeling of sorrow and concern for someone who is suffering or unlucky
senses.definitionCN: 对正在受苦或遭遇不幸的人产生的难过与关切
senses.example: He looked at the injured bird with pity.
senses.exampleCN: 他怜悯地看着那只受伤的鸟。
senses.why: Latin pietas began as dutiful loyalty toward the gods and one's family, and Christian writers bent it toward tender concern for the weak, which is the feeling English now calls pity.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 pietas 起初指对神明与家人尽责的忠诚，基督教文献把它弯向对弱者的温柔关切；英语接过的正是这份「心里为别人发软」的感觉，所以怜悯义带着「本该关怀」的底色。

senses.title: A cause for mild regret
senses.definition: something that is a shame or a cause for mild regret
senses.definitionCN: 令人觉得惋惜、可惜的事
senses.example: It is a pity that the concert was cancelled.
senses.exampleCN: 音乐会取消了，真可惜。
senses.why: When sympathy is aimed at a situation rather than a person, it cools into mild regret, and the fixed phrase a pity carries that lighter, almost polite disappointment.
senses.whyCN: 当同情不是对着某个人，而是对着一件事，它就降温成轻微的惋惜；固定说法 a pity 承载的正是这种较轻、几乎带点客气的失望。

senses.title: To feel sorry for someone
senses.definition: to feel sorrow or sympathy for someone because of their suffering
senses.definitionCN: 因某人受苦而为他感到难过、同情
senses.example: I pity anyone who has to work outside in this weather.
senses.exampleCN: 这种天气还得在户外干活的人，我替他们难过。
senses.why: English often turns a feeling into a verb without changing its form, so the noun of compassion became a verb naming the act of feeling it.
senses.whyCN: 英语常把一种情感直接拿来当动词，词形不变；表示同情心的名词于是变成动词，指「生出这份同情」的动作。

intro.en: Pity comes from Latin pietas, dutiful loyalty, through French, and the religious duty softened into compassion before English took the word over.
intro.cn: pity 经法语来自拉丁语 pietas（尽责的忠诚）；那份宗教性的本分在进入英语之前，已经软化成同情。

items.en: Pius meant dutiful, loyal and reverent, first toward the gods and then toward family and country.
items.cn: pius 意为尽责的、忠诚的、虔敬的，最初对神明而言，后来也用于家人与国家。

items.en: Pietas named that dutiful loyalty; early Christian writers used it for compassionate devotion, and the emotional colour grew stronger.
items.cn: pietas 指这种尽责的忠诚；早期基督教作者用它来表示带着慈悲的虔敬，情感色彩因此变浓。

items.en: Old French pite took the word from Latin and made compassion its main sense.
items.cn: 古法语 pite 从拉丁语接过这个词，并把「怜悯」定为主要词义。

items.en: Middle English pite or pity meant tender sympathy and, in the phrase it is pity, also a matter for regret.
items.cn: 中古英语的 pite 或 pity 既指温柔的同情，也在 it is pity 这样的说法里指令人惋惜的事。

items.en: Modern English keeps the noun and the verb, and the everyday phrase a pity now often means simply what a shame.
items.cn: 现代英语保留了名词与动词两种用法，日常说法 a pity 如今常常就等于「真可惜」。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built on the same Latin stem; the near-meaning group gathers words for sympathy and for mild regret.
note.cn: 形近组收同一拉丁词干上的词；近义组收表示同情与轻微惋惜的词。

entries.definition: Arousing pity, or deserving contempt because it is so small or weak.
entries.definitionCN: 令人同情的，或因太小太弱而显得可鄙的。

entries.definition: Showing no pity at all; cruel and unfeeling.
entries.definitionCN: 毫不同情的；冷酷无情的。

entries.definition: Dutiful devotion, especially to religion; it shares the Latin root pietas.
entries.definitionCN: 尽责的虔敬，尤指对宗教的虔敬；与 pity 同出拉丁语 pietas。

entries.definition: A very small amount of money or food; it also descends from Latin pietas.
entries.definitionCN: 极少的一点钱或食物；同样源自拉丁语 pietas。

entries.definition: A deep awareness of another's suffering together with a wish to help.
entries.definitionCN: 对他人苦难的深切体会，以及想要帮助的愿望。

entries.definition: Shared feeling for someone's sorrow or trouble.
entries.definitionCN: 对他人悲伤或困境的共鸣。

entries.definition: A reason to feel regret about something that has happened.
entries.definitionCN: 对已发生之事感到惋惜的理由。

entries.definition: Kindness shown to someone who is in one's power to punish.
entries.definitionCN: 对处于自己掌控之下、本可惩罚者的仁慈与宽恕。

normalIntro.en: A Latin word for duty, a Christian shade of compassion and a French narrowing all lead to the double English life of sympathy and mild regret.
normalIntro.cn: 一个表示本分的拉丁词、一层基督教的慈悲色彩，再加上法语中的收窄，最终汇成英语里「同情」与「轻微惋惜」的双重用法。

normal.en: Latin pius meant dutiful, and pietas meant that duty; pity keeps the warmth of duty but loses the religious edge.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 pius 意为尽责的，pietas 意为这份本分；pity 保留了本分里的温度，却丢掉了宗教的锋利边缘。

normal.en: French pite narrowed the word to compassion before English borrowed it, so the emotional sense arrived first.
normal.cn: 法语 pite 在英语借入之前已把词义收窄到「怜悯」，所以情感义是最先到达的。

normal.en: The phrase a pity turns sympathy toward a fact rather than a person, which is why it means a shame rather than mercy.
normal.cn: a pity 把同情从人转向一件事，所以它的意思是「可惜」，而不是「宽恕」。

normal.en: Pitiful and pitiless split the same stem in opposite directions: one invites pity, the other refuses it.
normal.cn: pitiful 与 pitiless 把同一个词干拉向相反方向：一个招来怜悯，一个拒绝怜悯。

normal.en: The verb pity needs no ending of its own; it simply puts the noun form in front of an object.
normal.cn: 动词 pity 不必另加词尾，直接把名词形式放在宾语前面就行。

abstract.en: Pity is duty that has forgotten its rules and kept only its tenderness.
abstract.cn: 怜悯是忘了规矩、只留下温柔的那份本分。

abstract.en: The same word can look down at a wounded bird and shrug at a cancelled concert, because sorrow cools into regret when nobody is suffering.
abstract.cn: 同一个词既能低头看一只受伤的鸟，也能对一场取消的音乐会耸耸肩，因为当没有人正在受苦时，难过就降温成了惋惜。

abstract.en: Saying I pity you can comfort or condescend, which shows how close sympathy stands to distance.
abstract.cn: 说一句 I pity you，既可能是在安慰，也可能带着居高临下，可见同情与距离挨得有多近。

examples.en: He looked at the injured bird with pity.
examples.cn: 他怜悯地看着那只受伤的鸟。

examples.en: It is a pity that the concert was cancelled.
examples.cn: 音乐会取消了，真可惜。

examples.en: I pity anyone who has to work outside in this weather.
examples.cn: 这种天气还得在户外干活的人，我替他们难过。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「批踢」——看到挨批又被踢的人，忍不住生出同情；pity 就是怜悯与遗憾。

root: 拉丁语 pius（尽责的、虔敬的）构成 pietas（虔敬、忠诚），经古法语 pite 进入英语；同族词多与虔敬、同情以及「少得可怜的一点东西」有关。

sensesIntro.en: The core image is a hand reaching toward someone who is suffering; from that warmth come the noun of compassion, the verb of feeling it and the cooler regret of a pity.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心意象是一只手伸向正在受苦的人；同情心的名词、生出同情的动词，以及较冷的「a pity」之叹，都从这份温度里分出来。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a passer-by bending down in the rain to help a stranger gather a spilled bag.
core.cn: 核心意象：雨中的路人弯下腰，帮陌生人捡起散落一地的行李。

branches.en: a bird held in two careful hands
branches.cn: 双手小心捧着一只鸟

branches.en: a coat offered without being asked
branches.cn: 没被要求就递过去的外套

branches.en: a cancelled ticket lying on a table
branches.cn: 桌上放着作废的票

branches.en: the feeling and the act of feeling it
branches.cn: 同情心与生出同情的动作

branches.en: a small word for a small disappointment
branches.cn: 用一个轻词说一件小失望

intro.en: A Latin adjective of duty, its noun, a French form and two English suffixes that pull the word toward pity and away from it hold it together.
intro.cn: 一个表示本分的拉丁形容词、它的名词、一个法语形式，以及两个把词义拉向同情和拉离同情的英语后缀，共同撑起这个词。

latinIntro.en: The Latin ancestry is secure: pius supplies the adjective of duty and pietas the noun that French and English softened into compassion.
latinIntro.cn: 这一支的拉丁来历是可靠的：pius 提供表示本分的形容词，pietas 提供名词，二者经法语与英语软化成「怜悯」。

items.meaning: full of, having the quality of

definition_zh: 个人的；私人的；亲自的；涉及私生活的；人称的
definition_en: relating to one particular person rather than to others, or done by that person directly
core_image: 一只抽屉拉开一道缝，里面是只属于一个人的旧照片、钥匙和一封没寄出的信
scene: 搬家那天，纸箱上写着同一个名字，里面装着相册、旧信和一只用了多年的杯子，都是不打算与人分享的东西。 She keeps her personal letters in a locked drawer.
sceneCN: 这里是「个人的、私人的」（第 1 个义项：属于某一个人而非公共的）；句意为她把私人信件锁在抽屉里。画面里那只抽屉只为一个名字打开。

pos.zh: 个人的；私人的；亲自的；人称的

derivatives.zh: 由 personal 加 -ly 构成，义为「亲自；就个人而言」
由同一词干改接 -ity 构成，义为「性格；人格」
拉丁语 persona 经古法语进入英语，义为「人；个人」
由否定前缀 im- 加 personal 构成，义为「非个人的；没有人情味的」
由 personal 加动词后缀 -ize 构成，义为「使个性化」

senses.title: Belonging to one person alone
senses.definition: belonging to or used by one particular person and not shared with others
senses.definitionCN: 属于或供某一个特定的人使用，不与别人共有
senses.example: Please keep your personal papers in this folder.
senses.exampleCN: 请把你的私人文件放在这个文件夹里。
senses.why: The word starts from Latin persona, the mask that marked one character on stage, so anything personal is tied to a single someone.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从拉丁语 persona 出发，那是舞台上一个角色所戴的面具，因此凡是 personal 的东西都系在某一个具体的人身上。

senses.title: Done by the person himself or herself
senses.definition: done by the person directly rather than through someone else
senses.definitionCN: 由本人直接去做，而不是经由别人
senses.example: The director paid a personal visit to the family.
senses.exampleCN: 主任亲自上门探望了这家人。
senses.why: If something belongs to one person, it can also be what that person does with his own hands instead of sending a stand-in.
senses.whyCN: 既然某样东西可以专属一个人，也就可以指这个人亲手去做、不派代表的事，亲自义正是从所属义挪过来的。

senses.title: Concerning private feelings or private life
senses.titleCN: 涉及私生活的；针对个人的
senses.definition: touching on someone's private life or feelings, often in a way that feels intrusive
senses.definitionCN: 触及某人的私生活或感情，常带冒犯、探究的意味
senses.example: The reporter asked a personal question about her marriage.
senses.exampleCN: 记者问了一个涉及她婚姻的私人问题。
senses.why: Once the word marks the area that belongs to one person, a question entering that area is felt as a crossing of the line.
senses.whyCN: 这个词先划出属于一个人的地盘，问题一旦踏进这块地盘，就被感受为越界，于是带上冒犯、探私的色彩。

senses.title: Showing grammatical person
senses.definition: used in grammar for forms that show whether the speaker, the listener or a third party is meant
senses.definitionCN: 语法中用来表明所指的是说话人、听话人还是第三方的形式
senses.example: In English the personal pronouns change form between subject and object.
senses.exampleCN: 英语的人称代词在主格和宾格之间会变形。
senses.why: Grammarians needed a label for the forms that shift with who is speaking, and persona already meant the role a speaker takes.
senses.whyCN: 语法学家需要给随说话人而变的词形起个名字，而 persona 本来就有「所扮演的角色」之意，正好拿来用。

intro.en: Personal comes from Latin persona, a mask and the role worn with it; the adjective personalis was built on that noun and reached English through French.
intro.cn: personal 来自拉丁语 persona，指面具以及随面具而来的角色；形容词 personalis 由这个名词构成，经法语进入英语。

items.en: Persona named the mask an actor wore and, by extension, the character played; its earlier origin is uncertain and may be Etruscan.
items.cn: persona 指演员戴的面具，进而指所扮演的角色；它更早的来源不确定，可能与伊特鲁里亚语有关。

items.en: Late Latin formed personalis, meaning of a person, on the noun persona.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语在 persona 之上构成 personalis，意为属于某个人的。

items.en: Old French carried the adjective as personel, still close to the sense of belonging to a particular person.
items.cn: 古法语以 personel 的形式使用这个形容词，仍保留属于某个特定人的意思。

items.en: Middle English personal appears in the fourteenth century, first in legal and religious writing about the rights of one person.
items.cn: 中古英语的 personal 出现在十四世纪，最早见于讨论个人权利的法律与宗教文献。

items.en: Modern English extends it to privacy, to doing something oneself, and to grammar, where it labels the pronouns of speaker and listener.
items.cn: 现代英语把它扩展到隐私、亲自做事，以及语法中标记说话人与听话人的代词。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words on the Latin noun for a mask and a role; the near-meaning group gathers adjectives of what belongs to one person.
note.cn: 形近组收建立在表示面具与角色的拉丁名词上的词；近义组收表示属于某一个人的形容词。

entries.definition: A single human being, the noun from which the adjective was built.
entries.definitionCN: 一个单独的人，是构成这个形容词的名词。

entries.definition: The set of qualities that make a person distinctive.
entries.definitionCN: 使一个人与众不同的那组特质。

entries.definition: The adverb built on the adjective, meaning in one's own body or in one's own view.
entries.definitionCN: 由这个形容词构成的副词，意为亲自或就本人看来。

entries.definition: Without human warmth, or without reference to any particular person.
entries.definitionCN: 缺乏人情味，或不指向任何具体的人。

entries.definition: Belonging to one person and kept from public view.
entries.definitionCN: 属于一个人、不向公众公开的。

entries.definition: Relating to one single person, seen apart from the group.
entries.definitionCN: 与单个的人有关、被从群体中单独看待的。

entries.definition: Used to stress that something belongs to the person just mentioned.
entries.definitionCN: 用来强调某物属于刚提到的那个人。

entries.definition: Very close and private, said of feelings and relationships.
entries.definitionCN: 形容感情与关系时指非常亲密而私密的。

normalIntro.en: A Latin mask, a Latin adjective ending and two English suffixes carry the idea of one person from the stage to grammar.
normalIntro.cn: 一个拉丁语的面具、一个拉丁语形容词词尾和两个英语后缀，把一个人的念头从舞台一路带到语法。

normal.en: Persona was a stage mask, so personal still carries the sense of one particular face rather than a crowd.
normal.cn: persona 本是舞台面具，所以 personal 至今带着某一张具体的脸、而不是一群人的意味。

normal.en: Person is the noun, personal the adjective, personally the adverb: one meaning in three jobs.
normal.cn: person 是名词，personal 是形容词，personally 是副词：一个意思，三种岗位。

normal.en: Impersonal adds the negative prefix and takes the human warmth away.
normal.cn: impersonal 加上否定前缀，就把人情味拿走了。

normal.en: A personal pronoun is the one place where grammar openly asks who is speaking.
normal.cn: 人称代词正是语法公开追问谁在说话的地方。

normal.en: Personal belongings and private belongings overlap, but personal stresses the owner while private stresses the closed door.
normal.cn: 个人物品与私人物品意思相近，但 personal 强调归属，private 强调关起来不让人看。

abstract.en: A mask that becomes a person: the word itself shows how a role hardens into an identity.
abstract.cn: 从面具变成人：这个词的来历本身就说明一个角色如何凝固成一个身份。

abstract.en: Personal is a line drawn around one body; whatever is inside the line may be shared, but only by permission.
abstract.cn: personal 是在一具身体周围画下的线；线内的一切都可以分享，但必须经过允许。

abstract.en: When a rule is called impersonal, it is being blamed for not seeing the faces it applies to.
abstract.cn: 当一条规则被说成没有人情味，其实是在责怪它看不见自己所管辖的那些脸。

examples.en: She packed her personal belongings into two boxes.
examples.cn: 她把个人物品装进两个箱子。

examples.en: He never discusses his personal life with colleagues.
examples.cn: 他从不与同事谈论自己的私生活。

examples.en: This is a personal letter, not a public statement.
examples.cn: 这是一封私人信件，不是公开声明。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「泼森呢」——下雨天只有一把破伞，撑开也只够护住自己一个人；personal 就是个人的、私人的。

root: 拉丁语 persona（面具、角色，更早来源不确定）构成晚期拉丁语 personalis，经古法语 personel 进入英语；同族词多与人、身份有关。

sensesIntro.en: The word begins with one person and spreads outward: what that person owns, what that person does, what is private, and finally who is speaking in a sentence.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词从一个「人」出发向外扩：属于这个人的东西、这个人亲自做的事、只属于他的私密领域，最后是句子里标明谁在说话的形式。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a drawer pulled open a little, showing a photograph, a key and a letter that belong to one person only.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只抽屉拉开一道缝，里面是只属于一个人的旧照片、钥匙和一封没寄出的信。

branches.en: a drawer with a name written inside the lid
branches.cn: 抽屉盖内侧写着一个名字

branches.en: a director standing at a doorstep himself
branches.cn: 主任自己站到了门口

branches.en: a question that makes the room go quiet
branches.cn: 一个让全场安静下来的问题

branches.en: a pronoun pointing back at the speaker
branches.cn: 一个代词指回说话人

branches.en: things that belong to you and things you do yourself
branches.cn: 属于你的东西与你亲自做的事

intro.en: A Latin mask, a Latin adjective ending and two English suffixes let one word name a person, a private thing and a grammatical role.
intro.cn: 一个拉丁语面具、一个拉丁语形容词词尾和两个英语后缀，让同一个词既能指人、又能指私人之物，还能指语法角色。

latinIntro.en: The Latin source is recorded as persona and personalis; the earlier origin of persona itself remains uncertain.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语来源可查为 persona 与 personalis；不过 persona 更早的出处并不确定。
